items.title: Engine oil and filter
items.summary: The basic 10,000 mile or 12 month service. The drain plug is at the front of the pan and the small spin-on filter hides above and behind it, under a black plastic duct.

parts.note: Jaguar service sheet renews the plug and sealing washer every time. One UK owner reports the seal is not sold on its own.

consumables: Engine oil, 6.0 L service fill up to VIN A00366 and 7.0 L from VIN A00367 on, including all 4.2 cars
safety: Never work under the car on a jack alone. Use stands on firm level ground, chock the wheels that stay down, and put the box in Park.
Do not jack on the aluminium front crossbeam, and do not lift the car by one front wheel. The crossbeam, steering rack and brake pipes can all be damaged.
Hot oil burns. Let the engine cool for a while before you pull the plug.

steps.title: Warm and raise
steps.text: Run the engine for a few minutes so the oil flows, then switch off. Raise the front on ramps or jack centrally, on a wood or rubber pad, under the front body crossmember, which is the steel lower crossmember right at the front of the car, the one the towing eye screws into, not the aluminium suspension crossbeam behind it, and set stands at the sill jacking points. The wheels can stay on.
steps.warn: Never jack on the aluminium crossbeam.
steps.tip: One owner suggests raising the rear a little instead so the pan drains towards the plug at the front. Either works.

steps.title: Open the filler
steps.text: Lift the bonnet and take off the oil filler cap so the oil drains freely.

steps.title: Remove the duct
steps.text: Undo the single bolt holding the black plastic alternator cooling duct under the front of the engine and take the duct off. This is what hides the filter. Some cars have already lost theirs.

steps.title: Drain
steps.text: Set the pan under the plug, undo it with a 13 mm six-point socket and let the oil run until it drips.
steps.check: Look at the old oil for metal flakes or a milky look.

steps.title: Swap the filter
steps.text: The filter is small, so use wrench 303-752, or a strap wrench that closes down far enough. Spin it off, wipe the mating face on the filter head, and smear clean oil on the new seal. Spin the new filter on and tighten to 18 Nm exactly.
steps.tip: Check the old seal came off with the filter.

steps.title: Refit the plug
steps.text: Fit the new plug and washer and tighten to 30-40 Nm on a 4.0 or 25 Nm on a 4.2. Refit the duct.

steps.title: Fill
steps.text: Lower the car to level. Pour in the oil, starting a little short of the listed capacity. Cap it, run the engine for a minute, switch off, wait for the oil to settle and read the dipstick. Top up to the mark.
steps.warn: Go by the stick, not the jug.

warnOn.text: Owners quote 7.6 to 7.8 L for the 4.2 where Jaguar's book says 7.0 L. A dipstick change is also reported.

verify: No drips at the plug or filter after a run to temperature
Oil level on the dipstick mark with the car level
Oil warning light out within seconds of starting

diy.suits: A good first job. If you can use a socket and get the car safely on stands or ramps, you can do this.
diy.stop: Stop if the drain plug will not turn or its thread feels loose, or if you cannot get the car safely off the ground.

items.title: Air filter element
items.summary: A two-clip cover job once the intake pipe is off. Take your time with the plastic breather tube, which cracks with age.
consumables: Clean rag to cover the throttle body opening
safety: Stop dirt falling into the throttle body once the pipe is off. Cover the opening with a clean rag.

steps.title: Free the breather
steps.text: Pull the crankcase breather tube off the intake pipe or cam cover. Do not bend the tube. Inspect it for cracks while it is off.

steps.title: Remove the outlet pipe
steps.text: Slacken the clip at the throttle body and at the air box. On the 4.0, also undo the two bolts above the throttle body. Lift the pipe away and put a rag over the throttle body.

steps.title: Unplug the MAF
steps.text: Disconnect the plug on the mass air flow sensor. Leave the sensor in the cover and do not touch its wire.

steps.title: Open the box
steps.text: Release the air box cover clips. A long screwdriver helps with the two inboard clips. Lift the cover and take out the element.

steps.title: Fit the new element
steps.text: Wipe out the box, seat the new element squarely and clip the cover down.

steps.title: Refit the pipe
steps.text: Reconnect the MAF plug. Remove the rag, seat the pipe fully on the throttle body and air box and tighten the clips (4.2: 5 Nm. No figure sourced for the 4.0.) Do not use lubricant on the pipe. Refit the breather.
steps.warn: An air leak after the MAF upsets fuelling. Check both ends are fully seated.

verify: Engine idles normally with no new warning
Pipe does not move at either clip

diy.suits: Anyone. It is a few clips and one intake pipe.
diy.stop: Stop if the plastic breather tube cracks, or if the engine runs badly afterwards. An air leak upsets the fuelling.

items.title: Front brake pads
items.summary: Do both sides: pads come in axle sets. Standard calipers slide on two guide pins and the housing comes off to reach the pads. Brembo cars drop their pads out through pins and R clips with the caliper left in place. Minimum pad thickness is 2 mm.

parts.note: One axle set. Inner pad has a clip into the piston.

consumables: Brembo cars: brake grease Molykote Cu 7439 for the backplate shoulders
safety: Never work under the car on a jack alone. Use stands on firm level ground, chock the wheels that stay down, and put the box in Park.
Do not jack on the aluminium front crossbeam, and do not lift the car by one front wheel. The crossbeam, steering rack and brake pipes can all be damaged.
Brake dust is a health risk. Remove it with a vacuum brush, not an air line.
Brake fluid strips paint. Rinse any spill straight away with clean water.
Pads are replaced in axle sets, both sides at once.
Many X100 nuts and bolts use thread-locking features that limit reuse. Renew any self-locking fastener that spins on easily.

steps.title: Prepare the reservoir
steps.text: Open the bonnet and fit wing covers. Loosen the brake fluid reservoir cap and wrap a cloth around the reservoir to catch overflow.

steps.title: Raise the front
steps.text: Handbrake on, box in Park, chock the rear wheels. Slacken the front wheel nuts. Put the trolley jack, with a wood or rubber pad on its head, centrally under the front body crossmember and lift. That is the steel lower crossmember right at the front of the car, the one the towing eye screws into, not the aluminium suspension crossbeam behind it. Set stands at the two sill jacking points just behind the front wheels, lower onto them, and take the front wheels off.
steps.warn: Jack on the body crossmember, never on the aluminium suspension crossbeam. The Vehicle Care book says not to use jacking equipment under the front cross member, without saying which one. Jaguar's workshop text puts the jack on the body crossmember and forbids the aluminium suspension crossbeam, so that is the one to keep off. No photo confirms this reading: if you cannot tell them apart, stop and read the Jacking page.

steps.title: Remove the caliper housing
steps.text: Do one side, then repeat on the other, up to refitting the wheels. Unclip the anti-rattle spring, pull the dust covers off the guide pins, undo both pins and lift the caliper housing off the caliper carrier. Tie it up with stiff wire, so its weight does not hang on the brake hose.
steps.warn: Do not let the caliper hang on its hose.

steps.title: Remove the pads
steps.text: Take the pads out of the housing. The inner pad is held into the piston by a clip. Discard them.
steps.check: Under 2 mm of friction means they were overdue. Inspect the disc while you are here.

steps.title: Remove the pads
steps.text: Do one side, then repeat on the other, up to refitting the wheels. Remove the R clips, withdraw the pins, take off the anti-rattle spring and pull out the pads. Leave the caliper bolted on. Disturbing the other caliper bolts upsets its factory alignment to the disc.
steps.warn: Do not loosen any caliper bolt other than the anchor bracket bolts, and those only if the caliper has to come off.

steps.title: Clean
steps.text: Vacuum off the dust with the vacuum brush. Then clean all mating surfaces and the piston face with brake cleaner on a cloth.

steps.title: Push the piston back
steps.text: Slowly push the piston back into the housing with the piston retract tool. Watch the reservoir, which can overflow as the fluid comes back.
steps.warn: Mop any spilled fluid off the paint immediately with clean water.

steps.title: Fit new pads
steps.text: Peel the backing paper to expose the adhesive shim, then push the inner pad clip into the piston and fit the outer pad.

steps.title: Fit new pads
steps.text: Put an even layer of brake grease on the backplate shoulders, keeping it off the friction face and disc. Fit each pad with its arrow following forward wheel rotation, then the anti-rattle spring, pins and R clips. Repeat on the other side.
steps.warn: The direction arrow must follow wheel rotation.

steps.title: Refit the caliper
steps.text: Seat the housing on the caliper carrier, tighten the guide pins to 25-30 Nm, refit the dust covers and clip on the anti-rattle spring. Repeat on the other side.

steps.title: Refit wheels and lower
steps.text: Refit the front wheels and run the nuts up by hand. Raise off the stands, lower to the ground and torque the nuts to 88-102 Nm in a star pattern.
steps.check: Every nut clicks at 88-102 Nm.

steps.title: Pump the pedal
steps.text: Before moving the car, start the engine and press the pedal repeatedly until it firms up. Check the reservoir is at MAX, take off the cloth and fit the cap.
steps.warn: The first press goes to the floor. Do this before the car moves.

verify: Pedal firm and high before moving
Short road test with gentle bedding-in stops
No drag: wheels spin freely when jacked

diy.suits: A careful beginner, with someone experienced to check the work. Brakes are not a job to guess at.
diy.stop: Stop if a bolt will not move, a hose looks damaged, or the pedal is not firm before you drive. Never drive with a soft pedal.

items.title: Rear brake pads
items.summary: Do both sides: pads come in axle sets. Same layout as the front on a smaller caliper. Rear standard calipers use guide pins. Brembo rears use pins with collets and no R clips.

parts.note: One axle set.

consumables: Brembo cars: brake grease Molykote Cu 7439
safety: Never work under the car on a jack alone. Use stands on firm level ground, chock the wheels that stay down, and put the box in Park.
Brake dust is a health risk. Remove it with a vacuum brush, not an air line.
Brake fluid strips paint. Rinse any spill straight away with clean water.
Pads are replaced in axle sets, both sides at once.
Many X100 nuts and bolts use thread-locking features that limit reuse. Renew any self-locking fastener that spins on easily.

steps.title: Prepare the reservoir
steps.text: Open the bonnet, fit wing covers, loosen the reservoir cap and wrap a cloth around it.

steps.title: Raise the rear
steps.text: Box in Park, chock the front wheels. Slacken the rear wheel nuts. Put the jack centrally under the rear suspension subframe with a block of wood on the jack head and lift. Set stands at the two sill jacking points just ahead of the rear wheels, lower onto them, and take the rear wheels off.
steps.warn: Use the wood block. The jack head must not bear directly on the subframe.

steps.title: Remove the caliper housing
steps.text: Do one side, then repeat on the other, up to refitting the wheels. Unclip the anti-rattle spring, pull off the dust covers, undo the guide pins, lift the housing off the caliper carrier and tie it aside.
steps.warn: Do not let the caliper hang on its hose.

steps.title: Remove the pads
steps.text: Take the pads out of the housing. The inner pad clips into the piston.

steps.title: Remove the pads
steps.text: Do one side, then repeat on the other, up to refitting the wheels. Withdraw the pins, take off the anti-rattle spring and remove the pads with the caliper left in place.
steps.warn: Leave the caliper bolts alone. Its alignment to the disc is set at first fitting.

steps.title: Clean and retract
steps.text: Clean the mating surfaces and piston face with brake cleaner on a cloth. Slowly push the piston back with the piston retract tool while watching the reservoir.

steps.title: Fit new pads
steps.text: Peel the backing paper from the shim, push the inner pad clip into the piston and fit the outer pad.

steps.title: Fit new pads
steps.text: Grease the backplate shoulders, follow the direction arrow, fit the spring and push the pins home until the collets engage fully. Repeat on the other side.

steps.title: Refit the caliper
steps.text: Seat the housing, tighten the guide pins to 25-30 Nm, fit the dust covers and anti-rattle spring. Repeat on the other side.

steps.title: Refit wheels and lower
steps.text: Refit the rear wheels and run the nuts up by hand. Raise off the stands, lower to the ground and torque the nuts to 88-102 Nm in a star pattern.
steps.check: Every nut clicks at 88-102 Nm.

steps.title: Pump the pedal
steps.text: Start the engine and press the pedal repeatedly until firm. Check the reservoir is at MAX and fit the cap.

verify: Rear wheels turn freely with the handbrake off

diy.suits: A careful beginner, with someone experienced to check the work. Brakes are not a job to guess at.
diy.stop: Stop if a bolt will not move, a hose looks damaged, or the pedal is not firm before you drive. Never drive with a soft pedal.

items.title: Cabin pollen filter
items.summary: Under the plenum cover at the base of the windscreen. Wiper arms and the plenum cover come off first. Filter fitted where the market specified one.
safety: Lay a cloth on the screen before the wiper arms come off. A sprung arm can crack the glass.

steps.title: Protect the wings
steps.text: Open the bonnet and lay covers over both wings.

steps.title: Remove wiper arms
steps.text: Take off the wiper arms and blades.
steps.tip: Mark the parked position on the screen with tape so they go back square.

steps.title: Remove plenum cover
steps.text: Take off the plenum cover to reach the filter housing.

steps.title: Release the filter
steps.text: Release the two tangs at the top of the filter and tilt it forward. Release the two lower tangs, press the accelerator cable support gently clear, and lift the element out.

steps.title: Fit the new filter
steps.text: Fit the new element with the white flocked side facing forward. If it will not go in that way round it is the wrong part. Seat the lower edge past the tangs and cable support, lift the top tangs and press the top rearward until it sits home.
steps.warn: White flocked side faces the front of the car.

steps.title: Rebuild
steps.text: Refit the plenum cover and the wiper arms and blades.

verify: Wipers park in the original position and sweep clear of the scuttle

diy.suits: Anyone with a little patience. The fiddly part is getting the wiper arms off without marking the car.
diy.stop: Stop if a wiper arm will not lift off. Forcing it can crack the windscreen.

items.title: Battery check and parasitic drain test
items.summary: Owners find these cars need a strong, healthy battery. The battery lives in the boot. After 60 minutes asleep the car should draw under 30 mA.

parts.note: Only if it fails.

safety: Batteries give off explosive gas. No flame, wear eye protection, and ventilate the boot.
Note the radio code and presets first. Fault codes and learned idle values go when the battery is disconnected.
Audio code savers keep the system live. Do not use them on airbag or fuel work.
Engine off before disconnecting the battery.

steps.title: Reach the battery
steps.text: Lift the boot floor covering and take off the battery cover.

steps.title: Check resting voltage
steps.text: With the car parked for some hours, read the voltage across the terminals. Charge fully before going further. A weak battery makes this test meaningless.

steps.title: Drop the glass, set up the meter
steps.text: Take the key out. Open the door or doors so the glass drops, and keep them open until the battery is disconnected and the meter is in circuit. Jaguar prefers a clamp probe round the battery lead, which needs no disconnecting. If you use a meter, set it to the 10 A DC range or higher with the leads in the current sockets.
steps.warn: Jaguar warns that the electronic throttle on the XK8 can draw more than most meter fuses take.

steps.title: Put the meter in series
steps.text: Disconnect the negative cable. Connect the meter between the negative post and the cable. Do not crank the engine or switch on anything big through the meter.
steps.warn: Stay on the 10 A range or higher. Do not crank, and do not drop to the low mA range until the current has fallen, or you will blow the meter's fuse.

steps.title: Put the car to sleep
steps.text: With the meter in circuit, switch the ignition on, then off, without cranking. Take the key out. Close or latch the doors and arm the car, so everything reads as shut.
steps.warn: Do not open a door from now on. That fires the window drop motors through the meter.
steps.tip: The battery is in the boot, so plan how you will leave it open without keeping modules awake. If the reading stays high, rule out the boot light and boot switch first.

steps.title: Wait 60 minutes
steps.text: Leave the car alone for the full 60 minute shutdown period. Jaguar's figure for the X100 is under 30 mA after that time. Trackers and added accessories raise it.
steps.check: Under 30 mA is healthy.

steps.title: Find the circuit
steps.text: If it is high, clamp the meter round each junction box lead in turn, or measure the small voltage drop across each fuse. The circuit that shows the current is your culprit.
steps.warn: Pulling a fuse wakes modules and takes about 45 minutes to settle again. It can also reset the fault, so it goes undiagnosed.

steps.title: Reconnect
steps.text: Remove the meter, refit the negative cable and battery cover. Leave the battery off for at least 30 seconds in all, then reconnect the ground cable with one clean, firm contact and tighten to 4 Nm. Ignition on. Reset each window: hold the switch down for 5 seconds past the bottom stop, then up for 5 seconds past the top stop. Re-enter the radio code and set the clock.

verify: Charging voltage healthy with the engine running

diy.suits: Someone happy to use a meter and careful around a battery.
diy.stop: Stop if the reading stays high and you cannot find why. An auto electrician can trace it.

items.title: Spark plugs, 4.0 and 4.2
items.summary: Eight plugs under two coil covers. All have to come out from the top. On later cars the plugs are iridium with a 100,000 mile life. Early 4.0 cars use a different plug and a wider gap, so check the variant note before buying.
consumables: Dielectric grease for the coil boots, sparingly
Anti-seize only if you choose to follow JagRepair: see the warning on the torque step
safety: Work on a cold engine. Aluminium heads strip threads when hot.
Keep the plug wells clean. Blow out grit before the plug comes out so nothing falls in the cylinder.

steps.title: Clear the top of the engine
steps.text: NA cars: take off the oil filler cap and pull off the engine cover, then refit the cap loosely to keep dirt out.

steps.title: Remove the right bank intake
steps.text: For the right bank, remove the air cleaner outlet pipe as in the air filter job. Do not bend or force the pipe, and inspect it for cracks.

steps.title: Take off the coil cover
steps.text: Undo the small bolts and lift off the coil-on-plug cover on each bank. A bolt that turns but will not come out has lost its nut below. Pull up gently while you turn.

steps.title: Pull the coils
steps.text: Unplug each coil, take out its fixing and ease it straight up. A stuck rubber boot can be wiggled off with long-nose pliers. Work one bank at a time so the coils stay in order.
steps.tip: The 4.0 coil is held by two bolts.
steps.check: Look down each well. Oil here means a cam cover seal or overfilling. The oil filler side is prone to overfill residue, so rule that out first.

steps.title: Remove the plugs
steps.text: Blow the well clean. Unscrew each plug with a magnetic or rubber-gripped plug socket and a long extension.

steps.title: Check the gap
steps.text: Iridium plugs on 2000 on cars use a 0.9-1.0 mm gap. The plug listed for 1998 and 1999 cars uses 1.2-1.3 mm. The manual for 4.2 cars gives 1 mm and NGK IFR-5N10. Do not lever on an iridium tip.
steps.warn: Check your plug against the VIN table. Early cars differ.

steps.title: Fit new plugs
steps.text: Start each plug by hand with the socket and extension until it runs down freely. Tighten to 27 Nm. Jaguar's spec book gives 28 Nm, so either figure is within the wrench's accuracy.
steps.warn: JagRepair used anti-seize on the threads. It reduces friction, so the same torque clamps harder. If you use it, keep it thin and do not exceed the figure.

steps.title: Refit coils
steps.text: Put a trace of dielectric grease in the boots. Press each coil on until it seats, tighten its fixing to 5 Nm and plug it in.

steps.title: Close up
steps.text: Refit the coil covers, the intake pipe and the engine cover. While the pipe is off, check the breather stub is clear.

verify: No misfire codes after a road test
No air leak at the intake pipe

diy.suits: A patient owner with a torque wrench. It takes time more than skill.
diy.stop: Stop if a plug stays tight all the way out, or a new one will not start by hand. A damaged thread in the aluminium head is a garage repair.

items.title: Coil-on-plug replacement
items.summary: One coil per cylinder, a quick swap once the cover is off. A misfire on one cylinder is easy to test by swapping a coil to another bank position and seeing if the fault moves.

parts.note: Per failed coil. Connector type differs across years, so check before buying.

safety: Switch the ignition off before unplugging any coil.

steps.title: Read the code
steps.text: Read the misfire code to find the cylinder. Viewed from the driving seat, the right-hand bank is A bank and the left-hand bank is B bank.

steps.title: Clear the way
steps.text: NA cars: remove the oil filler cap and engine cover. Right bank: remove the air cleaner outlet pipe and, on the factory sequence, the air cleaner element.

steps.title: Remove the coil cover
steps.text: Undo the small bolts and lift off the coil cover.

steps.title: Swap the coil
steps.text: Unplug the coil, take out the fixing and ease the coil up off the plug. Push the new coil on until it seats and tighten to 5 Nm.
steps.check: Inspect the boot for tracking and the well for oil.

steps.title: Rebuild
steps.text: Plug in, refit the cover and whatever came off to reach it.

verify: Misfire code cleared and stays cleared after a road test

diy.suits: Most owners. It is a quick swap once the cover is off.
diy.stop: Stop if the misfire stays after a new coil. The cause is somewhere else, and a garage can test for it.

items.title: Brake fluid change and bleed
items.summary: Fresh DOT 4 every two years. Bleed left front, right front, left rear, right rear. Brembo calipers have an inner and an outer nipple on each side. The factory method is pedal bleeding, so a helper is the simplest route.
consumables: Clear bleed hose and catch bottle
safety: Brake fluid strips paint. Rinse any spill straight away with clean water.
Wash your hands after handling brake fluid. If it gets in your eyes, flush with cold running water and seek help if irritation stays.
Never work under the car on a jack alone. Use stands on firm level ground, chock the wheels that stay down, and put the box in Park.
Do not use ITT Super DOT 4 on 2006 model year cars. Shell ESL Super DOT 4 is the replacement and suits all years.

steps.title: Raise the car
steps.text: Jaguar does this on a four-post lift with the wheels on. At home, raise the car level on four stands at the sill jacking points and take the wheels off for access.
steps.warn: Jack points only. See the front and rear raising steps in the pad jobs.

steps.title: Fill the reservoir
steps.text: Fill the reservoir to MAX. Keep it above MIN throughout. Top it up every few pumps. If you let air in you start again.

steps.title: Left front first
steps.text: Take the cap off the left front nipple and fit the bleed hose into a bottle. Helper presses the pedal, you open the nipple, the helper pushes to the floor, you close it, the helper lets go. Wait two seconds for the master cylinder to prime. Repeat until clean fluid with no bubbles comes out.

steps.title: Brembo: two nipples
steps.text: High performance calipers have two nipples per caliper. Do the outer nipple first, then the inner, at each corner.
steps.tip: Fit two hoses and two bottles.

steps.title: Tighten the nipple
steps.text: Standard calipers: 4-6 Nm at the front and 8-11 Nm at the rear. Brembo calipers: 12-16 Nm at both ends. These are small numbers, so go gently.

steps.title: Work round the car
steps.text: Repeat in this order: left front, right front, left rear, right rear.

steps.title: Finish
steps.text: Fill to MAX and fit the cap. Start the engine, check pedal travel and firmness. Hold the pedal down and walk round looking for leaks.
steps.check: Pedal stays high and firm with the engine running.

verify: Firm pedal with the engine running
No wet nipples or unions under pedal pressure
Slow test stop before any road speed

diy.suits: Someone careful who has done brake pads, with a helper for the pedal or a one-person bleeding kit.
diy.stop: Stop if the pedal stays soft or the reservoir runs dry. Do not drive the car: call a garage or a mobile mechanic.

items.title: Front brake discs and pads
items.summary: Discs are held by the wheel and clamped to the hub. Always fit new pads with new discs, in pairs. Standard front discs are 305 mm or 325 mm depending on the car, both 28 to 28.5 mm thick new and 26 mm minimum. Naturally aspirated cars change at VIN 037348; check before buying. Brembo fronts are 355 mm, 32 mm new, 30 mm minimum.

parts.note: New pads every time discs change.

safety: Never work under the car on a jack alone. Use stands on firm level ground, chock the wheels that stay down, and put the box in Park.
Do not jack on the aluminium front crossbeam, and do not lift the car by one front wheel. The crossbeam, steering rack and brake pipes can all be damaged.
Brake dust is a health risk. Remove it with a vacuum brush, not an air line.
Brake fluid strips paint. Rinse any spill straight away with clean water.
Brake discs are always replaced in pairs.
Many X100 nuts and bolts use thread-locking features that limit reuse. Renew any self-locking fastener that spins on easily.

steps.title: Prepare the reservoir
steps.text: Open the bonnet, fit wing covers, loosen the reservoir cap and wrap a cloth around it.

steps.title: Raise the front
steps.text: Handbrake on, box in Park, chock the rear wheels. Slacken the front wheel nuts. Put the trolley jack, with a wood or rubber pad on its head, centrally under the front body crossmember and lift. That is the steel lower crossmember right at the front of the car, the one the towing eye screws into, not the aluminium suspension crossbeam behind it. Set stands at the two sill jacking points just behind the front wheels, lower onto them, and take the front wheels off.
steps.warn: Jack on the body crossmember, never on the aluminium suspension crossbeam. The Vehicle Care book says not to use jacking equipment under the front cross member, without saying which one. Jaguar's workshop text puts the jack on the body crossmember and forbids the aluminium suspension crossbeam, so that is the one to keep off. No photo confirms this reading: if you cannot tell them apart, stop and read the Jacking page.

steps.title: Remove caliper and pads
steps.text: Unclip the anti-rattle spring, remove the dust covers and guide pins, lift off the caliper housing and tie it up with stiff wire. Take out the pads and discard them.
steps.warn: Never hang the caliper on its hose.

steps.title: Remove the caliper carrier
steps.text: Undo the two carrier bolts at the vertical link and take the caliper carrier off.

steps.title: Remove the disc
steps.text: Pull the disc off the hub. Clean the hub face right back to bright metal. Rust here causes run-out.
steps.check: Maximum installed run-out is 0.1 mm, so the hub face matters.

steps.title: Fit the disc
steps.text: Fit the new disc and check run-out with a dial gauge. Limit 0.1 mm.

steps.title: Refit the caliper carrier
steps.text: Fit the caliper carrier and tighten the bolts to the figure below for your car.

steps.title: Fit pads and caliper
steps.text: Slowly push the piston back with the piston retract tool, clean its face, peel the shim backing and fit the pads. Seat the housing, tighten the guide pins to 25-30 Nm, refit the dust covers and spring. Repeat on the other side.

steps.title: Refit wheels and lower
steps.text: Refit the front wheels and run the nuts up by hand. Raise off the stands, lower to the ground and torque the nuts to 88-102 Nm in a star pattern.
steps.check: Every nut clicks at 88-102 Nm.

steps.title: Pump the pedal
steps.text: Start the engine and press the pedal repeatedly until firm. Check the reservoir, remove the cloth and fit the cap.
steps.warn: Do this before the car moves.

verify: No pulsing through the pedal on test stops

diy.suits: A careful owner who has already done pads, with someone experienced to check the work.
diy.stop: Stop if a bolt will not move, a hose looks damaged, or the pedal is not firm before you drive. Never drive with a soft pedal.

items.title: Rear brake discs and pads
items.summary: The handbrake shoes run inside the rear disc, so the adjuster must be backed off through an access hole before the disc comes off, then reset afterwards. Standard rear discs are 305 mm, 19.5 to 20 mm new, 18.5 mm minimum. Brembo rears are 330 mm, 28 mm new, 26 mm minimum.

parts.note: New pads every time discs change.

safety: Never work under the car on a jack alone. Use stands on firm level ground, chock the wheels that stay down, and put the box in Park.
Brake dust is a health risk. Remove it with a vacuum brush, not an air line.
Brake fluid strips paint. Rinse any spill straight away with clean water.
Brake discs are always replaced in pairs.
Many X100 nuts and bolts use thread-locking features that limit reuse. Renew any self-locking fastener that spins on easily.

steps.title: Prepare the reservoir
steps.text: Open the bonnet, fit wing covers, loosen the reservoir cap and wrap a cloth around it.

steps.title: Raise the rear
steps.text: Box in Park, chock the front wheels. Slacken the rear wheel nuts. Put the jack centrally under the rear suspension subframe with a block of wood on the jack head and lift. Set stands at the two sill jacking points just ahead of the rear wheels, lower onto them, and take the rear wheels off. Handbrake off and box in Neutral once the car is safely on stands, so the discs can turn.
steps.warn: Use the wood block. The jack head must not bear directly on the subframe.

steps.title: Remove caliper and pads
steps.text: Unclip the anti-rattle spring, remove the dust covers and guide pins, take the housing off the caliper carrier and tie it up with stiff wire. Take the pads out.
steps.warn: Never hang the caliper on its hose.

steps.title: Remove the caliper carrier
steps.text: Undo the two bolts and take the caliper carrier off the hub carrier.

steps.title: Back off the handbrake
steps.text: Pull the plug from the access hole in the disc and turn the disc until the hole lines up with the adjuster. Turn the adjuster clockwise to slacken the shoes.

steps.title: Remove the disc
steps.text: Lift the disc off the studs. Vacuum the dust from the caliper and shoes, then clean the hub face.
steps.check: Shoes have a 2 mm minimum thickness.

steps.title: Fit the disc
steps.text: Fit the new disc with the hub and disc access holes aligned.

steps.title: Set the handbrake shoes
steps.text: Lever released, box in Neutral. Hold the disc on with three wheel nuts at 20 Nm. Line up the hole with the adjuster. Use a flat screwdriver to turn the adjuster counter-clockwise until the disc locks. Then ease it clockwise until the disc just spins freely. Refit the plug.
steps.warn: The return spring must sit between the adjuster spokes, or the adjuster can wander.

steps.title: Check run-out
steps.text: Dial gauge on the disc face. Limit is 0.15 mm on standard rear discs and 0.1 mm on Brembo.

steps.title: Refit carrier, pads, caliper
steps.text: Tighten the caliper carrier bolts to the figure below for your car. Push the piston back slowly with the piston retract tool, fit the pads with new shims, seat the housing, tighten the guide pins to 25-30 Nm, fit the dust covers and spring. Repeat on the other side.

steps.title: Refit wheels and lower
steps.text: Refit the rear wheels and run the nuts up by hand. Raise off the stands, lower to the ground and torque the nuts to 88-102 Nm in a star pattern.
steps.check: Every nut clicks at 88-102 Nm.

steps.title: Pump the pedal
steps.text: Start the engine and press the pedal until firm. Check the reservoir and fit the cap. Check the handbrake comes on in 3 to 5 clicks. If not, adjust the cable nut.

verify: Rear wheels spin freely with the lever down

diy.suits: Someone who has already done front brakes. The handbrake shoes inside the disc make this one fiddlier.
diy.stop: Stop if the disc will not come off with the adjuster backed off, or the handbrake does not hold afterwards.

items.title: Coolant drain, refill and bleed
items.summary: Drain from the plastic plug on the radiator, refill to MAX with a 50/50 mix, then bleed by running with the heater on full. Supercharged cars have a second fill point on the supercharger. Capacity is 9.5 L NA or 11.5 L SC. Use the coolant your car has: D985, D542 and orange XLC must never be mixed.

parts.note: Supercharged cars only.

consumables: Coolant concentrate meeting WSS M97B44-D, or the older D542 type on early cars, see warning
safety: Open the expansion tank cap only when the engine has cooled. Wrap it in a thick cloth, turn slowly, and step back while pressure escapes.
The cooling fan can start with the engine off when hot. Pull fuse 14 in the engine management fuse box before working near it, and refit it before starting.
Never work under the car on a jack alone. Use stands on firm level ground, chock the wheels that stay down, and put the box in Park.
Do not jack on the aluminium front crossbeam, and do not lift the car by one front wheel. The crossbeam, steering rack and brake pipes can all be damaged.

steps.title: Cold start only
steps.text: Let the engine cool. Pull fuse 14 from the engine management fuse box. Release the pressure and take off the expansion tank cap.
steps.warn: Hot coolant under pressure scalds.

steps.title: Raise the front
steps.text: Jack centrally, on a wood or rubber pad, under the front body crossmember, which is the steel lower crossmember right at the front of the car, the one the towing eye screws into, not the aluminium suspension crossbeam behind it,, set stands at the sill jacking points, and take off the lower alternator cooling duct.

steps.title: Drain
steps.text: Open the radiator drain plug and let it empty into a pan. It is a plastic plug at the bottom of the radiator with a cross head. One owner turned it with a very large washer.
steps.tip: The block has its own drain plug at the rear left side if you want the system fully empty.

steps.title: Close the drain
steps.text: Refit the plug and do not overtighten it. 4.2: only 1 Nm. No figure sourced for the 4.0. Wash any coolant off the underside, refit the duct and lower the car.

steps.title: First fill
steps.text: Fill to the MAX mark on the expansion tank with a 50/50 mix. Fit the cap.
steps.warn: D985, D542 and orange XLC (JLM 20972) must never be mixed. Check the VIN, the colour and the tank label before topping up.

steps.title: Supercharger fill
steps.text: Remove the filler plug on the supercharger coolant rail and discard its washer. Put a cloth round the port and top up. Switch the ignition on, without starting. The supercharger cooling pump runs, so keep adding coolant as the level drops. Switch off and fit the plug with a new washer (MY2000 on: 45 Nm. No figure sourced for earlier cars.)
steps.warn: Coolant can spit out of the port when the ignition goes on.
steps.tip: One owner describes this as a 3/4 inch inset plug.

steps.title: Run it hot
steps.text: Refit fuse 14. Start the engine with the cap on. Set the heater to max heat, blower to max and air to the dash vents. Run until hot air comes out, watching the gauge the whole time.
steps.warn: If the temperature rises above normal, switch off at once and let it cool.

steps.title: Top up cold
steps.text: Switch off and let it cool completely. Release the cap with care and fill to MAX with the 50/50 mix again.
steps.check: Level holds at MAX after the next cold start.

verify: Gauge sits at normal and the fans cycle
No drip at the radiator drain plug
Level still at MAX after a cooling cycle

diy.suits: A careful owner with stands, and the time to let the engine cool right down.
diy.stop: Stop if the temperature climbs or the heater stays cold after bleeding. Trapped air can overheat the engine.

items.title: Accessory drive belt, tensioner and idler
items.summary: On 2003-on cars a 3/8 inch square drive in the tensioner swings it counter-clockwise to release the belt. On 1997-2002 cars you use a spanner on the tensioner idler centre bolt, which is left-hand thread. On supercharged cars the small supercharger belt comes off first. Renew at 100,000 miles.

parts.note: Replace with the idler if the belt chatters or walks.

safety: Battery ground off first on NA cars, per the manual. Never run the engine with the belt off.
The tensioner spring is strong. Keep fingers clear as it swings back.
1997-2002 cars: the tensioner idler centre bolt is left-hand thread. Never put clockwise torque on it, or it can loosen.

steps.title: Doors open, battery off
steps.text: Open the driver's door, or both doors, so the frameless glass drops. Keep the doors open until the battery is disconnected. Then disconnect the battery ground cable in the boot.
steps.warn: With the glass still up and the battery off, shutting a door can foul the seal or the hood rail.

steps.title: Remove the supercharger belt
steps.text: Follow the supercharger belt job first.

steps.title: Remove the cover
steps.text: NA cars: take off the oil filler cap and engine cover.

steps.title: Release the belt, 1997-2002
steps.text: Put a spanner, JD-230 or Snap-on XDHM 1415, on the centre bolt of the tensioner idler pulley and turn the assembly to the left, viewed from the front, against the spring. Slip the belt off the alternator pulley, ease the tensioner back and take the spanner off.
steps.warn: That centre bolt is left-hand thread. Never apply clockwise torque to it, or it can loosen.

steps.title: Release the belt, 2003 on
steps.text: Fit a 3/8 inch square drive bar in the tensioner and rotate it counter-clockwise. Slip the belt off and let the tensioner return gently.

steps.title: Change the tensioner
steps.text: Undo the tensioner bolt if it needs to come off and move it clear. 4.0: tensioner bolt 38-48 Nm, idler bolt 53-69 Nm. 4.2: tensioner bolt 40 Nm, idler bolt 45 Nm.
steps.warn: The 4.2 manual disagrees with itself on the idler: 45 Nm in the engine table, 40 Nm in the accessory table, 25 Nm in the front cover job.

steps.title: Fit the belt
steps.text: Route the belt round all pulleys, swing the tensioner and slip it on. Check every rib sits in its groove.
steps.check: Spin each pulley by hand first. A rough or noisy bearing is now easy to find.

steps.title: Refit the supercharger belt
steps.text: Supercharged cars: refit the supercharger belt as in its own job.

steps.title: Refit
steps.text: NA cars: refit the engine cover.

steps.title: Reconnect and relearn
steps.text: Leave the battery off for at least 30 seconds in all, then reconnect the ground cable with one clean, firm contact and tighten to 4 Nm. Ignition on. Reset each window: hold the switch down for 5 seconds past the bottom stop, then up for 5 seconds past the top stop. Re-enter the radio code and set the clock. Let the engine computer relearn: idle to full temperature, switch off, restart and idle for 2 minutes, hold 2 minutes in Drive on the brake, then drive about 5 miles of varied roads.

verify: Belt tracks straight with no chatter at idle

diy.suits: A careful owner with the right tool for the tensioner. You work from above, so no jacking up.
diy.stop: Stop if the idler bolt will not move. On 1997-2002 cars it is left-hand thread, so turning it the normal way only tightens it.

items.title: MAF sensor clean or replace
items.summary: Unplug it and clean the hot wire with MAF cleaner only. The sensor is expensive, so clean it only when you have a reason. Do not touch the wire.

parts.note: Only if cleaning does not help.

consumables: MAF cleaner spray. Nothing else. No throttle body cleaner.
safety: Keep throttle body cleaner away from the MAF.

steps.title: Remove the intake pipe
steps.text: Unclip the breather tube, slacken the clip at the MAF and remove the air cleaner outlet pipe. On the 4.0 there are two bolts over the throttle body.

steps.title: Lift off the sensor
steps.text: Unclip the air box cover and unplug the MAF. On a straight replacement, undo the sensor screws and lift it out.

steps.title: Clean
steps.text: Spray MAF cleaner on the element several times and let it dry. Touch it with nothing except the spray.
steps.warn: The wire is fragile. One touch can write the sensor off.

steps.title: Refit
steps.text: Refit the sensor with its screws at 2 Nm. Refit the box lid and plug. Seat the intake pipe, tighten the clips (4.2: 5 Nm. No figure sourced for the 4.0.) and refit the breather.
steps.check: Any air leak after the MAF will give lean fault codes.

verify: Fuel trims settle on a scan tool
Codes stay clear after a road test

diy.suits: Most owners. It is one sensor, one plug and a can of the right cleaner.
diy.stop: Stop if the fault comes back after cleaning. The sensor wire is fragile and a new sensor is expensive, so have it tested first.

items.title: Throttle body clean
items.summary: A wipe of the bore and blade edge through the intake opening, with the throttle body left on the car. Breather carbon sticks the blade, and owners report restricted performance warnings clearing after a clean. Owner guidance only: this manual has no cleaning procedure.
consumables: Throttle body cleaner safe for coated bores
safety: Ignition off and the key out. The throttle motor is strong and can trap fingers.
Spray onto the rag, not into the bore. Do not spray into a running engine.
Keep the cleaner off the MAF sensor.

steps.title: Key out
steps.text: Switch off and take the key out of the car.

steps.title: Remove the intake pipe
steps.text: Unclip the breather tube, slacken the clips and take off the air cleaner outlet pipe. On the 4.0 undo the two bolts above the throttle body.

steps.title: Open the blade by hand
steps.text: Move the throttle blade by hand far enough to reach behind it. On cable cars one owner turns the cable spindle to open it. Do not touch or change the idle stop. One owner found the car would not idle after moving it.

steps.title: Clean the edge
steps.text: Wet the rag with cleaner and wipe the blade edge and the bore where the blade seats. That edge is the part that matters. The curved bore below the blade does not need attention.
steps.warn: Early bores and blades have a molybdenum coating. Use a cleaner that will not strip it, and wipe gently.

steps.title: Rebuild
steps.text: Refit the intake pipe, tighten the clips (4.2: 5 Nm. No figure sourced for the 4.0.) and refit the breather. Clean the part-load breather at the same time if it is due.

verify: Idle steady after a few minutes
Throttle returns freely with the key off

diy.suits: A careful owner who accepts the risk. This is owner advice: Jaguar gives no procedure.
diy.stop: Stop if the blade does not move freely, or warning lights appear afterwards. Early bodies have a coating, so wipe gently.

items.title: Anti-roll bar drop links, front and rear
items.summary: A quick fix for knocks over rough roads. Hold the ball pin flats with an open spanner so the rubber boot does not twist. Rear links use bushes, not ball joints.

parts.note: Front pair
Rear pair, with upper and lower bushes

safety: Never work under the car on a jack alone. Use stands on firm level ground, chock the wheels that stay down, and put the box in Park.
Do not jack on the aluminium front crossbeam, and do not lift the car by one front wheel. The crossbeam, steering rack and brake pipes can all be damaged.
Many X100 nuts and bolts use thread-locking features that limit reuse. Renew any self-locking fastener that spins on easily.

steps.title: Raise the front
steps.text: Handbrake on, box in Park, chock the rear wheels. Slacken the front wheel nuts. Put the trolley jack, with a wood or rubber pad on its head, centrally under the front body crossmember and lift. That is the steel lower crossmember right at the front of the car, the one the towing eye screws into, not the aluminium suspension crossbeam behind it. Set stands at the two sill jacking points just behind the front wheels, lower onto them, and take the front wheels off.
steps.warn: Jack on the body crossmember, never on the aluminium suspension crossbeam. The Vehicle Care book says not to use jacking equipment under the front cross member, without saying which one. Jaguar's workshop text puts the jack on the body crossmember and forbids the aluminium suspension crossbeam, so that is the one to keep off. No photo confirms this reading: if you cannot tell them apart, stop and read the Jacking page.

steps.title: Front link: top nut
steps.text: Hold the ball pin flats with an open spanner so the dust cover does not twist. Undo the nut at the anti-roll bar.

steps.title: Front link: lower bolt
steps.text: Remove the nut and bolt at the lower wishbone and lift the link away.
steps.check: Inspect the bar bushes while you are here.

steps.title: Fit the front link
steps.text: Fit the bolt at the wishbone and tighten the nut to 39-55 Nm. Fit the link to the bar, hold the flats and tighten the nut to 60-80 Nm.
steps.warn: Hold the flats while torquing or the boot tears.

steps.title: Refit wheels and lower
steps.text: Refit the front wheels and run the nuts up by hand. Raise off the stands, lower to the ground and torque the nuts to 88-102 Nm in a star pattern.
steps.check: Every nut clicks at 88-102 Nm.

steps.title: Rear link
steps.text: Jaguar works on the rear links with the car on a four-post lift, so the suspension stays loaded. Ramps do the same job at home. Remove the nut at the wishbone and the lower bush, then the nut and bolt at the bar. Take the link down and strip the upper bush.

steps.title: Fit the rear link
steps.text: Fit the upper bush, offer up the link and fit the nut and bolt at the bar. Fit the lower bush and nut at the wishbone. Both tighten to 30-40 Nm.

verify: Links not bound at full droop

diy.suits: A careful owner with stands and a torque wrench. A good first suspension job.
diy.stop: Stop if a nut spins with its ball pin and will not hold, or a rubber boot tears.

items.title: Thermostat and housing
items.summary: The thermostat itself is a simple swap on every car: a cover and a new seal. On 4.0 NA cars the plastic thermostat housing is the known weak point, and its two rear bolts sit under the intake manifold, so changing the housing is the harder job. An aluminium replacement is a common upgrade.

parts.note: 4.0 cars if plastic. Replaces with a new seal set.
Always new.

consumables: New hose clips, as new hoses are thicker and old clips fight back
safety: Open the expansion tank cap only when the engine has cooled. Wrap it in a thick cloth, turn slowly, and step back while pressure escapes.
The cooling fan can start with the engine off when hot. Pull fuse 14 in the engine management fuse box before working near it, and refit it before starting.
Never work under the car on a jack alone. Use stands on firm level ground, chock the wheels that stay down, and put the box in Park.

steps.title: Drain
steps.text: Drain the cooling system as in the coolant job and lower the car.

steps.title: Replace the thermostat, 4.0 NA
steps.text: Engine cover off. Disconnect the bottom hose at the thermostat cover. Remove the three cover bolts, then the cover and thermostat. Discard the seal and fit a new one; it goes on either way round. Refit so the vent ball locates in the recess in the cover, or on earlier cars with the vent pin at the top. Tighten the bolts to 8-10 Nm. If you are not changing the housing as well, skip to the hoses and refill.
steps.warn: Vent ball or pin must go to the recess or the top.

steps.title: Replace the thermostat, 4.0 SC
steps.text: On the supercharged 4.0 the thermostat sits in the coolant outlet pipe with its own cover. Disconnect the bottom hose from the pipe. Remove the three cover bolts, then the cover, thermostat and seal. Discard the seal. Refit with new sealing rings on the outlet pipe and housing, with the ball valve in the recess in the cover, and tighten to 8-10 Nm.
steps.warn: Ball valve must locate in the recess.

steps.title: Make room for the housing
steps.text: 4.0 NA: remove the upper hose, undo the lower hose at the top, unplug the two fan connectors, undo the two fan shroud bolts and lift the fan assembly out. This also opens up the lower clamp.

steps.title: Remove the outlet pipe
steps.text: 4.0: take off the water outlet pipe to reach the housing.

steps.title: Undo the front bolts
steps.text: 4.0: the two front housing bolts come out easily with an 8 mm socket and an extension.

steps.title: Undo the rear bolts
steps.text: 4.0: the two rear bolts sit under the front of the intake manifold. Bend a cheap 8 mm open spanner close to the head, a little longer than you think. Lift up on the housing as you work, which loads the bolts and helps them turn.
steps.tip: Slotting the bolt heads lets a long screwdriver start them on refit. Replacement Allen head bolts with a ball-end key are another owner idea.

steps.title: Fit the new housing
steps.text: 4.0: fit new seals and a new housing. Start the rear bolts by screwdriver, then nip them with the open spanner. JTIS prints no torque for these housing bolts on a 4.0: its 8-10 Nm is for the cover bolts, and the 4.2 housing is 10 Nm. JagRepair says the rear pair could not be torqued, so hand judgement is needed. Do not reuse the old seals.

steps.title: Replace the thermostat, 4.2 NA
steps.text: Detach the coolant hose and remove the thermostat. Discard the O-ring. Refit with a new O-ring and tighten to 9 Nm.

steps.title: Replace the thermostat, 4.2 SC
steps.text: Detach the hose, remove the housing cover and thermostat. Discard the O-ring. On refit keep the thermostat bypass valve at 12 o'clock. Cover bolts are 9 Nm.
steps.warn: Bypass valve at 12 o'clock.

steps.title: Refit hoses and fan
steps.text: Refit the outlet pipe, hoses with new clips and the fan assembly. Reconnect the fan plugs.

steps.title: Refill and bleed
steps.text: Refill as in the coolant job: 50/50 mix to MAX, then on supercharged cars top up through the supercharger fill port with the ignition on. Run with the heater on full until hot air comes out, let it cool, and top up cold.
steps.warn: Do not run the engine with the expansion tank cap off.

verify: No weep at the housing after a hot and cold cycle
Gauge rises to normal and holds
Top hose soft when cold, not collapsing

diy.suits: Someone who has done a coolant change. The thermostat is simple, but on a 4.0 the housing bolts sit under the intake manifold.
diy.stop: Stop if a bolt shears or the old plastic housing breaks up. A broken bolt in the engine is a garage job.

items.title: Water pump
items.summary: An easy job on the front of the engine. Loosen the pulley bolts while the belt still holds the pulley. Pump bolts are torque plus angle. On the 4.2 the pulley bolts are also torque plus angle and one-use. 4.0 pulley bolts are a plain 10-14 Nm.

parts.note: Manual calls for gasket and O-ring. JagRepair found a new pump that came with a metal gasket and no O-ring.
4.2: always new.

safety: Open the expansion tank cap only when the engine has cooled. Wrap it in a thick cloth, turn slowly, and step back while pressure escapes.
The cooling fan can start with the engine off when hot. Pull fuse 14 in the engine management fuse box before working near it, and refit it before starting.
Never work under the car on a jack alone. Use stands on firm level ground, chock the wheels that stay down, and put the box in Park.
1997-2002 cars: the tensioner idler centre bolt is left-hand thread. Never put clockwise torque on it, or it can loosen.

steps.title: Drain
steps.text: Drain the cooling system as in the coolant job and lower the car.

steps.title: Supercharger belt, 4.0 SC
steps.text: Remove the supercharger drive belt first, as in the supercharger belt job.

steps.title: Crack the pulley bolts
steps.text: With the belt still on, loosen the three pulley bolts. The belt stops the pulley turning.

steps.title: Release the belt, 1997-2002
steps.text: Put a spanner, JD-230 or Snap-on XDHM 1415, on the centre bolt of the tensioner idler pulley and turn the assembly to the left against the spring. Slip the belt off the alternator pulley, ease the tensioner back and take the belt off the pump pulley.
steps.warn: That centre bolt is left-hand thread. Never apply clockwise torque to it.

steps.title: Release the belt, 2003 on
steps.text: Rotate the tensioner counter-clockwise with a 3/8 inch bar and slip the belt off the water pump pulley.

steps.title: Remove the pulley
steps.text: Take out the bolts and the pulley. 4.2: discard the bolts.

steps.title: Remove the pump
steps.text: Undo the five pump bolts and pull the pump off. Discard the gasket and O-ring. Clean the face on the engine down to bare metal.
steps.check: Inspect the old impeller for erosion and the bearing for play.

steps.title: Fit the new pump
steps.text: Fit the new gasket and O-ring. Bolt the pump on at 8 Nm plus 90 degrees.

steps.title: Fit the pulley, 4.2
steps.text: Fit the pulley with new bolts at 10 Nm plus 45 degrees. The final tightening is easiest once the belt is back on.
steps.warn: New bolts only.

steps.title: Fit the pulley, 4.0
steps.text: Fit the pulley and tighten the bolts to 10-14 Nm, with no angle stage.
steps.warn: An extra 45 degrees on a 10-14 Nm bolt risks shearing it.

steps.title: Refit the belt
steps.text: Swing the tensioner and refit the belt with every rib in its groove.

steps.title: Supercharger belt back, 4.0 SC
steps.text: Refit the supercharger belt as in its own job.

steps.title: Refill and bleed
steps.text: Refill as in the coolant job: 50/50 mix to MAX, then on supercharged cars top up through the supercharger fill port with the ignition on. Run with the heater on full until hot air comes out, let it cool, and top up cold.
steps.warn: Do not run the engine with the expansion tank cap off.

steps.title: Squeeze the hoses
steps.text: Once warm and pressurised, give the top hose and crossover pipe a gentle squeeze and look for leaks. A new pump often reveals the next weak plastic part.
steps.warn: Hot pressurised coolant and a moving fan and belt. Engine off, key out, fans clear, gloves on, keep your face away from the pipe, and never open the cap.
steps.tip: JagRepair found a 4 inch crack in the crossover pipe this way.

verify: No weep from the pump tell-tale or gasket

diy.suits: A careful owner who has done the drive belt and a coolant change.
diy.stop: Stop if a pump bolt feels close to shearing, or coolant leaks after the refill. Follow the tightening figures exactly.

items.title: Coolant crossover pipe
items.summary: A plastic Bakelite pipe at the front of the engine, joining the banks and carrying the temperature sensor. It cracks with age. Four bolts, three hoses and a plug. Buy new gaskets, as the old ones deform.

parts.note: One owner on a later car says a new pipe comes with a sensor and gaskets. Check what you are buying.

safety: Open the expansion tank cap only when the engine has cooled. Wrap it in a thick cloth, turn slowly, and step back while pressure escapes.
The cooling fan can start with the engine off when hot. Pull fuse 14 in the engine management fuse box before working near it, and refit it before starting.

steps.title: Drain some coolant
steps.text: Drain enough coolant to get the level below the pipe. Owners report less than half a gallon from the upper hoses.

steps.title: Unplug the sensor
steps.text: Unclip the temperature sensor plug gently. JagRepair broke the plug stay and had to use a wire tie.

steps.title: Disconnect the hoses
steps.text: Undo the three hoses.

steps.title: Remove the pipe
steps.text: Undo the four bolts and lift the pipe away.
steps.check: JagRepair found a crack about 4 inches long that only showed when the top hose was squeezed.

steps.title: Fit the new pipe
steps.text: Clean the faces, fit new gaskets and bolt the pipe on. Reconnect the hoses and the sensor plug.
steps.warn: No published torque was found for these bolts. The thermostat housing bolts next to them are 10 Nm on a 4.2.

steps.title: Refill
steps.text: Refill and bleed as in the coolant job.

verify: No weep when warm and pressurised

diy.suits: A careful owner who has done a coolant change. Expect the old pipe to be brittle.
diy.stop: Stop if a hose will not come free or the old pipe breaks up. No tightening figure is on record for these bolts, so do not force them.

items.title: Fuel filter
items.summary: The filter sits deep in the left rear wheel well area, forward of the wheel, on a bracket. Take the left rear wheel off to see it. Note the flow arrow. Fittings differ: the factory 1997-2002 procedure uses threaded unions on new seals at 26-34 Nm, and 2003-on cars use push-on connectors with a 4 Nm filter nut. Look at the fitting before you start.

parts.note: Check the fitting type before buying. Some replacements have screw fittings that do not match early quick-connect lines.
1997-2002 threaded unions only.

consumables: Blanking plugs for the open pipes on 1997-2002 cars
safety: Fuel stays under pressure long after switch-off. Release it first, work outdoors or well ventilated, keep sparks and phones away, and have a catch pan ready.
Never work under the car on a jack alone. Use stands on firm level ground, chock the wheels that stay down, and put the box in Park.
Open a door so the glass drops, then disconnect the battery ground. Earth the car, and keep the earth on until the job is done.
Check for leaks by eye after the job, under pressure.
Do not use an audio code saver on fuel work. The car stays live with one fitted.

steps.title: Doors open, battery off
steps.text: Open the driver's door, or both doors, so the frameless glass drops. Keep the doors open until the battery is disconnected. Then disconnect the battery ground cable in the boot.
steps.warn: With the glass still up and the battery off, shutting a door can foul the seal or the hood rail.

steps.title: Release fuel pressure, 1997-2002
steps.text: Ignition off. NA cars: take off the oil filler cap and engine cover. Find the valve on the fuel cross-over pipe at the front of the manifold and remove its cap. Put a cloth under it and stand a closed container by the car. Fit pressure tool 310-058 or an equivalent, run its bleed tube into the container and release the pressure as the tool maker says. Remove the tool and cloth and refit the cap.
steps.warn: Keep the bleed tube in the container, and close the lid afterwards.

steps.title: Release fuel pressure, 2003 on
steps.text: NA cars: take off the filler cap and engine cover. Remove the cap on the pressure release valve on the fuel rail. Shut the tap on gauge 310-012 fully clockwise, fit it to the valve, then open it fully counter-clockwise into a container.
steps.warn: Tap fully clockwise before fitting the tool, or fuel will spray.
steps.tip: Owners also pull the fuel pump fuse with the engine idling until it stalls. Nobody confirmed that doing it with the engine off relieves the pressure.

steps.title: Drain the tank, 1997-2002
steps.text: Drain the fuel tank with a hand-operated suction pump. Never use an electric pump.
steps.warn: Hand pump only. An electric pump is an ignition risk.

steps.title: Raise the rear
steps.text: Box in Park, chock the front wheels. Slacken the rear wheel nuts. Put the jack centrally under the rear suspension subframe with a block of wood on the jack head and lift. Set stands at the two sill jacking points just ahead of the rear wheels, lower onto them, and take the rear wheels off. Only the left rear wheel has to come off.
steps.warn: Use the wood block. The jack head must not bear directly on the subframe.

steps.title: Find the filter
steps.text: Look forward of the left rear wheel, deep in the well, for a bracket with two fuel lines. A heat shield partly hides it. On one 1998 car the owner found it was not where he expected, so trace the lines if you need to.

steps.title: Disconnect the lines, 1997-2002
steps.text: Look at the fittings first. The factory procedure shows threaded unions, but owners report quick connectors with white tabs on some early cars, and those come off as on a later car. For threaded unions: remove the clamp bolt and move the clamp clear of the filter. Put a container under the filter. Hold with one spanner and turn the union with another so the pipes take no strain. Undo the tank pipe first and let the residual fuel drain, then the underfloor pipe. Discard the seals and fit blanking plugs to the open pipes.
steps.warn: Catch pan under it. Rags on the floor.

steps.title: Disconnect the lines, 2003 on
steps.text: Disconnect the line to the fuel rail and the line from the tank. The manual covers quick release and spring lock couplings, and a disconnect tool handles the spring type. Expect a spoonful or so of fuel.
steps.warn: Catch pan under it. Rags on the floor.

steps.title: Remove the filter
steps.text: Lift the filter away and note the flow arrow. On 2003-on cars undo the bracket nut first, then slide the filter out of the bracket.

steps.title: Fit the new filter, 1997-2002
steps.text: Fit the new filter with its arrow pointing the same way. Take out the blanking plugs and fit new seals to both pipes. Hold with a second spanner and tighten the union nuts to 26-34 Nm. Tighten the bracket bolt to 5-7 Nm. If your car has quick connectors, push the lines home until they click and tug each one.
steps.warn: These unions carry full pressure. 4 Nm here, the later figure, is a pressurised fuel leak.

steps.title: Fit the new filter, 2003 on
steps.text: Fit the new filter with its arrow pointing the same way. Tighten the filter nut and bracket nut to 4 Nm. Push the lines home until they click.
steps.check: Tug each line to prove it has latched.

steps.title: Refit wheels and lower
steps.text: Refit the rear wheels and run the nuts up by hand. Raise off the stands, lower to the ground and torque the nuts to 88-102 Nm in a star pattern.
steps.check: Every nut clicks at 88-102 Nm.

steps.title: Prime and check
steps.text: Refit the valve cap and engine cover. Refill the tank if you drained it. Leave the battery off for at least 30 seconds in all, then reconnect the ground cable with one clean, firm contact and tighten to 4 Nm. Ignition on. Reset each window: hold the switch down for 5 seconds past the bottom stop, then up for 5 seconds past the top stop. Re-enter the radio code and set the clock. Switch the ignition on a few times to prime, then start. Check both joints by eye. Let the engine computer relearn: idle to full temperature, switch off, restart and idle for 2 minutes, hold 2 minutes in Drive on the brake, then drive about 5 miles of varied roads.
steps.warn: Any wet joint: stop and fix it before the car moves.

diy.suits: Someone comfortable working on fuel lines. Petrol under pressure is the real risk here.
diy.stop: Stop if you cannot release the pressure, or you see or smell a leak afterwards. Do not run the car.

items.title: Gearbox fluid and filter service
items.summary: Three gearboxes are fitted. 4.0 NA has the ZF 5HP24, 4.0 SC has the Mercedes W5A580, and all 4.2 cars have the ZF 6HP26. The two ZF boxes have no dipstick, and level is set through a fill plug at a controlled temperature. The W5A580 has a sealed dipstick tube and uses service dipstick 307-379. A drain changes only part of the fluid. Jaguar calls it filled for life. Owners disagree and change it.

parts.note: ZF 6HP26: pan, gasket and filter replaced together.
ZF 5HP24: separate filter.
ZF 5HP24.
W5A580: new locking pin for the dipstick tube plug.

consumables: Correct ATF for the box: see the fluid note on the fill step
Long gloves, the exhaust is close
safety: Never work under the car on a jack alone. Use stands on firm level ground, chock the wheels that stay down, and put the box in Park.
Stay clear of the propshaft and exhaust with the engine running under the car.
Hot exhaust sits next to the fill plug. Wear long gloves.
The car must be level, or the level reading is wrong. Four stands at the same height for draining, and a level drive-on ramp or the ground for selector cycling.
Overfilling is as bad as underfilling.
Never select R or D with a person in the seat of a car on four axle stands. The driven wheels spin if the brake is released.
Hot transmission fluid can cause severe burns.

steps.title: Doors open, battery off
steps.text: Open the driver's door, or both doors, so the frameless glass drops. Keep the doors open until the battery is disconnected. Then disconnect the battery ground cable in the boot.
steps.warn: With the glass still up and the battery off, shutting a door can foul the seal or the hood rail.

steps.title: Raise level
steps.text: Raise the car on all four sill points and keep it level. Put a big pan under the box.
steps.warn: Level matters here. Use four stands at matched heights, or a lift.

steps.title: Crack the fill plug first
steps.text: ZF boxes only. Loosen the fill plug before you open the drain, so you know you can refill. On the 6HP26 it takes Jaguar adaptor 307-452. Owners use an 8 mm hex socket with adapters or a ratcheting spanner, as no ordinary extension fits.

steps.title: Drain, 6HP26
steps.text: Remove the fill plug and washer, then the drain plug and washer. Fit a new washer to the drain plug and tighten to 8 Nm once it stops. If the fluid is very dirty or full of metal, stop: Jaguar calls for a new transmission plus cooler and lines.
steps.warn: Note how much comes out. You will put back about the same.

steps.title: Change pan and filter, 6HP26
steps.text: Remove the pan bolts and take the pan, gasket and filter off as one unit. Fit the new pan and tighten the bolts to 8 Nm. Fasteners are T27 on some cars and reportedly T40 on others.

steps.title: Drain and filter, 5HP24
steps.text: Remove the pan drain plug, then the pan on its T27 screws. Pull the filter. Fit a new filter at 5 Nm. Refit the pan at 10 Nm with a new gasket. Refit the M16 pan plug at 30 Nm. ZF lists the M18 housing plug at 35 Nm.

steps.title: Drain, W5A580
steps.text: XKR 4.0 only. Carefully remove the drain plug and discard the washer. The fluid can cause severe burns and this procedure leaves the converter full. Refit the plug with a new washer at 20-24 Nm.
steps.warn: Do not assume ZF steps apply. Fluid is Shell ATF 3403 M115, JLM 20292, 9.5 L maximum fill.

steps.title: Fill
steps.text: Pump fluid in through the fill hole. Cable-tie the pump to the car so your hands are free. Esso LT 71141 JLM 20237, 10.0 L maximum.
steps.warn: Use only the specified fluid. Jaguar is explicit on the M1375.4 box.

steps.title: Fill
steps.text: Pump fluid in through the fill hole. Jaguar refills 8 L after a drain. Cable-tie the pump to the car so your hands are free. Shell M1375.4 C2C 8432, 9.5 L NA or 10.05 L SC maximum.
steps.warn: Use only the specified fluid. Jaguar is explicit on the M1375.4 box.

steps.title: Reconnect
steps.text: Leave the battery off for at least 30 seconds in all, then reconnect the ground cable with one clean, firm contact and tighten to 4 Nm. Ignition on. Reset each window: hold the switch down for 5 seconds past the bottom stop, then up for 5 seconds past the top stop. Re-enter the radio code and set the clock. Do the relearn drive after the fluid work.

steps.title: Circulate
steps.text: 6HP26: lower the car to the ground, or better, onto a level drive-on ramp. Never do this on four axle stands with the rear wheels free. Parking brake on, box in P, engine running for 2 minutes with the fluid below 30 C. With your foot on the brake go through R and D, waiting three seconds in each, and back to P. Only then raise the car, level, for the fill plug.
steps.warn: Selecting R or D with the driven wheels free spins them if the brake is released.

steps.title: Fill and set the level, W5A580
steps.text: Have a diagnostic tool ready to read the fluid temperature, which only shows in D or R. Break off the locking plate on the dipstick tube plug, push the locking pin down into the plug, lift the plug out, push the pin through and discard it. Pour in about 4 L. Select P and start. Pour in about 3 L more. With the wheels on the ground or a level ramp, foot on the brake, cycle P to D, D to R, R to P. Push dipstick 307-379 down until it touches the pan, read it against the 25 C or 80 C marks to suit the fluid temperature, wipe with a lint-free cloth and repeat. Correct the level; excess must be taken out. Stop the engine, seat the plug and fit a new locking pin.
steps.warn: Do not cycle the selector on axle stands. Only the specified fluid.

steps.title: Set the level, 5HP24
steps.text: Stand the car level for at least 2 minutes with the fluid below 30 C, on the ground or a level drive-on ramp with enough room to reach the plug. Select Park and start. Check idle is 600-750 rpm. Take the level plug out. Foot on the brake, move the selector P to D, D to R, R to P, pausing at least 3 seconds in each. Top up with the specified fluid until it overflows at the plug. Wait for a trickle or one minute. Fit the plug at 35 Nm and check the fluid has not passed 50 C.
steps.warn: Hot fluid can cause severe burns. With the engine off the reading is false. Do not cycle the selector on axle stands.

steps.title: Set the level, 6HP26
steps.text: Jaguar reads temperature with its diagnostic tool. It must be below 30 C when you start and must not pass 50 C when you finish. With the engine running, take the fill plug out. If nothing runs out, add 0.5 L at a time until it does. Let it run until the flow almost stops, then fit the plug with a new washer.
steps.warn: Above 50 C you read low and overfill. If it goes past 50 C, stop, cool below 30 C and start again.
steps.tip: Without a scan tool, owners use an IR thermometer on the pan. One stopped at 47 C.

steps.title: Tighten the fill plug
steps.text: 6HP26 fill plug: 35 Nm at the plug. With adaptor 307-452 on a torque wrench the wrench reads less. Set the wrench to 35 multiplied by its effective length, divided by that length plus the adaptor length.

steps.title: Repeat if you want
steps.text: A drain leaves fluid in the converter. Owners do repeat drains, driving in between, to change most of it. Flushing has critics. A 1998 owner reports replacing over 90 percent over four passes. Finish with the relearn drive: idle to full temperature, switch off, restart and idle for 2 minutes, hold 2 minutes in Drive on the brake, then about 5 miles of varied roads.

verify: No drips at pan, plugs or cooler lines
Level rechecked at the correct temperature after a short drive

diy.suits: An experienced home mechanic. The level must be set with the car dead level, and some gearboxes need Jaguar tools.
diy.stop: Stop if you are not sure of the level, or the gearbox slips or will not select a gear. Too much fluid is as bad as too little.

items.title: Differential oil
items.summary: Jaguar calls it filled for life and gives no drain plug. The only access is the fill plug high on the back of the casing, in the top right corner viewed from behind the car. The usual method is a hand pump through the fill hole.
consumables: Shell Spirax Super TS 90, JLM 20255, about 1.9 L
safety: Never work under the car on a jack alone. Use stands on firm level ground, chock the wheels that stay down, and put the box in Park.
Level the car front to rear, or the measured refill will not be accurate.

steps.title: Raise level
steps.text: Raise the car on all four sill points, level.
steps.warn: Rear jack point goes on the subframe with a block of wood.

steps.title: Find the plug
steps.text: Stand behind the car and look at the back of the diff casing, upper right. It is a square-drive plug. 4.2 cars have an added plate in front of it, which makes it harder to reach.
steps.tip: Owners have gone in with a stack of extensions rather than drilling the boot floor. Some use a piece of square stock about an inch long in the plug, then a ratchet from the side.

steps.title: Remove the plug
steps.text: Clean around it and undo it.

steps.title: Pump out
steps.text: Feed a hand pump tube to the bottom of the casing and pump the oil into a measuring jug. Move the tube around to get as much as you can. Warm oil moves better.
steps.check: Measure what comes out. Jaguar's fill is 1.9 L in the spec book and 1.8 L in the 4.2 manual.

steps.title: Pump in
steps.text: Pump in the same amount of new oil.
steps.tip: A forum owner used synthetic 75W-140 to match the old oil's thickness. That is not the Jaguar spec.

steps.title: Refit the plug
steps.text: Refit the plug and tighten firmly. No torque was found for this plug.
steps.warn: No published torque: go by feel.

verify: No weep at the plug after a run

diy.suits: A careful owner with stands and a hand pump. There is no drain plug, and Jaguar calls this oil filled for life.
diy.stop: Stop if the fill plug will not turn. A rounded plug is a garage job, and no tightening figure is published for it.

items.title: Convertible hood pump and ram service
items.summary: The hood runs on a boot-mounted electro-hydraulic pump at about 110 bar. Most faults come from low fluid or leaking rams and hoses. The system bleeds itself. Rams are removed one side at a time, and the right ram carries the switches. Rebuilds are available.

parts.note: Only if failed.
Left and right differ. The right ram has two microswitches.
One per disconnected hose.

consumables: Pentosin CHF 11S hydraulic fluid (green). Early brown fluid should be flushed out.
safety: Disconnect the battery ground before opening the system.
Pressure can leave a hose. Crack fittings under a cloth, with the top raised by hand and the pump valve in manual, as the steps do it.
Keep hands clear of the hood linkage while it moves.
Hydraulic fluid marks trim. Lay cloths everywhere.

steps.title: Check and top up
steps.text: Open the right side of the boot and find the pump. Look at the tank level marks. The manual says upper mark top down, lower mark top up. JagRepair argues the top line is right in either position. Fill through the plug on top with a syringe. Do not drop the plug behind the pump.
steps.warn: The two sources disagree. If in doubt fill to the upper mark with the hood down and do not overfill.
steps.tip: Three-tier boot platforms make access tighter, but the pump can still stay in place.

steps.title: Fluid colour
steps.text: Brown fluid on a 1996 to about 1999 car means the old type. Change to Pentosin CHF 11S. Jaguar bulletin 501-33 replaces the fluid every two years, as reported by JagRepair.

steps.title: Lower the hood and strip the trim
steps.text: For a ram: power the hood fully down. Run the seat on that side fully forward. Open the door so the glass drops, then disconnect the battery and leave the door open until it is off. Remove the rear seat cushion and squab, rear quarter cappings and casings, and the rear speaker on premium audio cars.

steps.title: Open the pump valve
steps.text: Reach the pump through the boot right liner and turn the valve fully counter-clockwise to manual. Move the hood by hand to fully raised.
steps.warn: Move the linkage carefully. Do not force or bend it.

steps.title: Unpin the ram
steps.text: Remove the clip and pin holding the ram to the frame linkage. On the right ram unplug the harness.

steps.title: Free the bracket
steps.text: Ease the headlining rear quarter clear. Take out the lower screw of the bracket cover plate, ease the headlining back, then remove the other two. Move the ram clear of the half pivot and keep the wavy washer.

steps.title: Disconnect the hoses
steps.text: Put cloth under the ram. Mark each hose. Undo them, discard the O-rings, and plug both the hoses and the ram at once.
steps.warn: Mark the hoses. They must go back on the same ports.

steps.title: Rebuild or replace
steps.text: Send the ram for rebuild or fit a new one. JagRepair lists Top Hydraulics in Oregon for ram and latch rebuilds. Left and right are not the same.

steps.title: Refit the ram
steps.text: New O-rings on the hoses, hoses on the ram in their marked places. Wavy washer on the pivot, seat the ram, refit the cover plate and its upper screws. Tuck the headlining back and fit the lower screw. Plug in the right ram.

steps.title: Rejoin the linkage
steps.text: Extend the rod to the frame and fit the clip and pin. Move the hood down by hand. Turn the pump valve fully clockwise back to power. Leave the battery off for at least 30 seconds in all, then reconnect the ground cable with one clean, firm contact and tighten to 4 Nm. Ignition on. Reset each window: hold the switch down for 5 seconds past the bottom stop, then up for 5 seconds past the top stop. Re-enter the radio code and set the clock.
steps.warn: The hood will not run with the valve left open.

steps.title: Cycle and top up
steps.text: Run the hood up, down, up. The system bleeds itself. Check every joint for leaks. Top up the tank with a new filler O-ring, then rebuild the trim.
steps.check: Run the engine for full voltage while cycling, as Jaguar bulletin 501-11 advises.

verify: Three clean cycles, windows following correctly
Latch closes and warning goes out

diy.suits: An experienced owner with patience and plenty of cloths. The system works at high pressure.
diy.stop: Stop if a ram or hose leaks badly, or the hood moves unevenly after the work.

items.title: Door handle, lock and latch
items.summary: Door card off, water shedder peeled back, and you can reach the rods, handle and latch. Two separate tasks are here: outer handle, and latch with lock motor. Battery off first, or the door glass can move on you.

parts.note: With lock motor.
Always fit new studs.

consumables: Tape for the puddle lamp harness
Clean rags and degreaser for the shedder faces
safety: Disconnect the battery ground before reaching inside the door. Global open and close can move the glass with your hand in there.
Glass must be fully up before you start.

steps.title: Glass up, battery off
steps.text: Key to position II, run the glass fully up, key off. Remove the battery cover in the boot and disconnect the ground.
