steps.warn: Do this before any hand goes in the door.

steps.title: Escutcheon
steps.text: Hold the inner handle open, pop the screw cover, remove the screw and lift the escutcheon off. Let the handle return.

steps.title: Pocket screws
steps.text: Lift the mat at the back of the door pocket and remove the screw. Release the plastic stud on the trim at the front of the pocket with a plastic hook and remove the trim. Remove the switch pack screw and let the pack hang. Remove the casing to bracket screw.

steps.title: Door casing off
steps.text: Pop the eight casing studs. Hold the casing away, unplug the switch pack and puddle lamp, and lift the casing off.

steps.title: Water shedder
steps.text: Remove the two casing bracket bolts. Release the puddle lamp harness tape. Peel the main water shedder off and lay it on clean plastic, sticky side down. Move the second PVC shedder aside.

steps.title: Outer handle
steps.text: Disconnect the handle rod and the lock barrel link rod at the motor. Remove the two handle screws and take the handle out. Move the lock assembly to the new handle.
steps.tip: Lock barrel rod is on the driver's door only.

steps.title: Latch: free the runner
steps.text: If doing the latch, remove the glass rear runner lower screws. Mark the upper screw position, remove it and move the runner clear. Where fitted, remove the lock security shield.

steps.title: Latch: remove
steps.text: Disconnect the rods at the latch. Take out the three latch screws and move the unit for access. Unplug the motor connector. Set the inner handle to locked, unhook the cable outer from its bracket and the inner from the handle. Lift the latch and motor out.

steps.title: Latch: bench swap
steps.text: Undo the cover screw and remove the cover, releasing the upper boss. Undo the motor screws and unhook the motor from the operating arm. Fit the motor to the new latch and refit the cover.
steps.tip: JagRepair shows a repair of the door switch inside this unit, in photos, on a 2000 car.

steps.title: Latch: refit
steps.text: Set the handle to locked, connect the cable, plug in the harness and bolt the latch in with its three screws. Reconnect the rods. Refit the security shield and rear runner. Tighten the upper screw at your mark before the lower screws.
steps.warn: Check handle and lock function now, with the door open.

steps.title: Water shedder back
steps.text: Refit the PVC shedder. Surfaces must be clean, oil free and dry. Stick the main shedder from the top down. Tape the puddle harness in place and refit the casing bracket.

steps.title: Door casing back
steps.text: Fit new studs to the casing. Connect the switch pack and puddle lamp, press the studs home and refit the screws, pocket trim, mat and escutcheon. Reconnect the battery.
steps.check: If you disconnect the battery, the window drop may need resetting.

verify: Inner and outer handles release the latch
Central locking works from key and fob
Interior light goes out when shut

diy.suits: A patient owner. No heavy work, but a lot of small rods and clips inside the door.
diy.stop: Stop if the door will not latch or open properly. Test it with the door open before you shut it.

items.title: Door window regulator and motor
items.summary: The glass is taped up at the top of the door while the regulator comes out through the aperture. The channel stud must go back exactly where it was, or the glass alignment is lost. Measure it first.

parts.note: Moves across if still good.
Always fit new studs.

safety: Battery ground off once the glass is down. Global open and close can catch your hand in the door.
Have a helper hold the glass when you lower it onto the regulator.

steps.title: Glass down, battery off
steps.text: With the door open, key to position II and run the glass fully down. Key off. Disconnect the battery ground.

steps.title: Strip the door
steps.text: Remove the door casing as in the door handle job. Remove the speaker, the main water shedder, and move the second shedder clear of the regulator.

steps.title: Free the glass
steps.text: Take the clips off the nylon fixings and keep them. Release the regulator from the fixings. Lift the glass by hand to the top and tape it to the top of the door with strong linen tape.
steps.warn: Tape it well. A dropped door glass breaks.

steps.title: Measure the stud
steps.text: Reach through the speaker hole and unplug the motor. With vernier calipers measure where the regulator channel stud sits in its slotted hole and write it down. Then remove the nut.
steps.warn: This measurement sets the glass alignment.

steps.title: Take it out
steps.text: Remove the motor to door screws. Lower the assembly into the bottom of the door, close the scissors and turn it to pass through the aperture.

steps.title: Swap the motor
steps.text: On the bench remove the motor from the regulator and fit it to the new one.

steps.title: Refit
steps.text: Close the scissors and pass the assembly back in. Fit the motor screws and channel nut loosely. Set the stud to your measurement and tighten the nut, then tighten the motor screws.

steps.title: Rejoin the glass
steps.text: Support the glass and take the tape off. Lower it onto the regulator, press the ball joints into the nylon seats and fit the clips. Connect the motor.

steps.title: Close up
steps.text: Refit the speaker with a new gasket, the shedders and door casing. Reconnect the battery and reset the window.

verify: Window drops and rises correctly on door open and close
Seals to the hood or roof without wind noise

diy.suits: A patient owner with a helper to hold the glass.
diy.stop: Stop if the glass binds or sits crooked. Its position is set by a measurement, and a garage can reset it.

items.title: Alternator
items.summary: Belt off from the top, the lower bolt and cooling ducts from below, the upper bolt from above again. Supercharged cars also have to move the supercharger water pump bracket.
safety: Disconnect the battery ground first. The alternator output stud is always live.
Never work under the car on a jack alone. Use stands on firm level ground, chock the wheels that stay down, and put the box in Park.
Do not jack on the aluminium front crossbeam, and do not lift the car by one front wheel. The crossbeam, steering rack and brake pipes can all be damaged.
1997-2002 cars: the tensioner idler centre bolt is left-hand thread. Never put clockwise torque on it, or it can loosen.

steps.title: Doors open, battery off
steps.text: Open the driver's door, or both doors, so the frameless glass drops. Keep the doors open until the battery is disconnected. Then disconnect the battery ground in the boot. NA cars: take off the oil filler cap and engine cover.
steps.warn: With the glass still up and the battery off, shutting a door can foul the seal or the hood rail.

steps.title: Clear the front, 4.0
steps.text: Remove the air cleaner assembly, then the fan and motor assembly from behind the radiator.

steps.title: Detach the belt, 1997-2002
steps.text: Put a spanner, JD-230 or Snap-on XDHM 1415, on the centre bolt of the tensioner idler pulley and turn the assembly to the left against the spring. Slip the belt off the alternator pulley and ease the tensioner back.
steps.warn: That centre bolt is left-hand thread. Never apply clockwise torque to it.

steps.title: Detach the belt, 2003 on
steps.text: Put a 3/8 inch drive bar in the tensioner, rotate it counter-clockwise and slip the belt off the alternator.

steps.title: Raise the front
steps.text: Jack centrally, on a wood or rubber pad, under the front body crossmember, which is the steel lower crossmember right at the front of the car, the one the towing eye screws into, not the aluminium suspension crossbeam behind it, and set stands at the sill jacking points.
steps.warn: Never jack on the aluminium crossbeam.

steps.title: Ducts off
steps.text: Remove the lower and upper alternator cooling ducts.

steps.title: Unplug from below
steps.text: Move the battery cable shroud aside, undo the battery cable nut and unplug the alternator connector. 4.0: also disconnect the suppression module positive and negative cables and move that harness clear.

steps.title: Lower bolt
steps.text: Remove the lower alternator nut and bolt, then lower the car.

steps.title: Upper bolt, 4.2
steps.text: Supercharged cars: detach the supercharger water pump bracket. Remove the upper bolt and lift the alternator out.

steps.title: Upper bolt, 4.0
steps.text: Remove the upper bolt. Work the alternator forward towards the radiator, turn it, and lift it out upwards between the engine and the radiator.

steps.title: Fit the new unit, 4.2
steps.text: Fit the alternator from above with the upper bolt at 21 Nm. Raise the car again for the lower nut and bolt at 40 Nm, the battery cable nut at 12 Nm and the plug.

steps.title: Fit the new unit, 4.0
steps.text: Ease the spacing bush rearwards a little in the mounting bracket, using a bolt, tube spacer and nut. Lower the alternator in between the engine and radiator and fit the upper bolt loose from above. Raise the car again. Fit the lower bolt and nut at 38-48 Nm, the suppression module cables, main cable, boot and plug. Lower the car and tighten the upper bolt to 18-24 Nm.

steps.title: Rebuild
steps.text: Refit the ducts with the car still raised, then lower the car. Refit the belt, the engine cover on NA cars, and on 4.0 cars the fan and air cleaner.

steps.title: Reconnect and relearn
steps.text: Leave the battery off for at least 30 seconds in all, then reconnect the ground cable with one clean, firm contact and tighten to 4 Nm. Ignition on. Reset each window: hold the switch down for 5 seconds past the bottom stop, then up for 5 seconds past the top stop. Re-enter the radio code and set the clock. Let the engine computer relearn: idle to full temperature, switch off, restart and idle for 2 minutes, hold 2 minutes in Drive on the brake, then drive about 5 miles of varied roads.

verify: Charging voltage healthy at the battery with the engine running

diy.suits: Someone with a good tool set and stands. You work from above and below, in tight space.
diy.stop: Stop if a bolt will not move, or the battery warning stays on afterwards. The alternator's main lead is always live, so disconnect the battery first.

items.title: Supercharger belt
items.summary: A short separate belt. Jaguar's tool 303-631 unloads the tensioner. See the service schedule for its interval.

parts.note: If rough.

safety: Disconnect the battery ground first.
Keep hands out of the fan area.

steps.title: Doors open, battery off
steps.text: Open the driver's door, or both doors, so the frameless glass drops. Keep the doors open until the battery is disconnected. Then disconnect the battery ground.
steps.warn: With the glass still up and the battery off, shutting a door can foul the seal or the hood rail.

steps.title: Unplug the fan
steps.text: Disconnect the right cooling fan connector.

steps.title: Release the belt
steps.text: Use tool 303-631 to unload the tensioner and slip the belt off.

steps.title: Move the tensioner
steps.text: Loosen the tensioner bolt and move the tensioner to pull the belt out.
steps.tip: Spin the pulleys by hand while the belt is off.

steps.title: Fit the belt
steps.text: Fit the belt, reposition the tensioner and tighten its bolt. MY1998: 39-51 Nm. 4.2: 40 Nm. No figure sourced for MY1999 to 2002. Reconnect the fan.

steps.title: Reconnect and relearn
steps.text: Leave the battery off for at least 30 seconds in all, then reconnect the ground cable with one clean, firm contact and tighten to 4 Nm. Ignition on. Reset each window: hold the switch down for 5 seconds past the bottom stop, then up for 5 seconds past the top stop. Re-enter the radio code and set the clock. Let the engine computer relearn: idle to full temperature, switch off, restart and idle for 2 minutes, hold 2 minutes in Drive on the brake, then drive about 5 miles of varied roads.

diy.suits: A careful owner with the Jaguar tensioner tool.
diy.stop: Stop if the tensioner will not release with the right tool. Do not lever it: the spring is strong.

items.title: Front dampers and springs
items.summary: Damper and spring come out as one assembly. The upper wishbone has to be swung out of the way to make room, so note the caster shims. Stripping the spring from the damper needs compressor 204-476, because the spring is under extreme tension. Handling pack and adaptive damping cars use different parts.

parts.note: Axle pair.
Rate depends on spec, and so does the packer count.
Always new.

safety: Never work under the car on a jack alone. Use stands on firm level ground, chock the wheels that stay down, and put the box in Park.
Do not jack on the aluminium front crossbeam, and do not lift the car by one front wheel. The crossbeam, steering rack and brake pipes can all be damaged.
Many X100 nuts and bolts use thread-locking features that limit reuse. Renew any self-locking fastener that spins on easily.
Keep the wishbone supported on a jack throughout. If it drops, the ball joints can be damaged.
Do not stretch the brake hose.
Strip the spring from the damper only in compressor 204-476 with the locking pin fully home. The spring is under extreme tension.

steps.title: Raise the front
steps.text: Handbrake on, box in Park, chock the rear wheels. Slacken the front wheel nuts. Put the trolley jack, with a wood or rubber pad on its head, centrally under the front body crossmember and lift. That is the steel lower crossmember right at the front of the car, the one the towing eye screws into, not the aluminium suspension crossbeam behind it. Set stands at the two sill jacking points just behind the front wheels, lower onto them, and take the front wheels off. Fit wing covers first.
steps.warn: Jack on the body crossmember, never on the aluminium suspension crossbeam. The Vehicle Care book says not to use jacking equipment under the front cross member, without saying which one. Jaguar's workshop text puts the jack on the body crossmember and forbids the aluminium suspension crossbeam, so that is the one to keep off. No photo confirms this reading: if you cannot tell them apart, stop and read the Jacking page.

steps.title: Support the wishbone
steps.text: Put a jack under the lower wishbone and raise it just until it takes the suspension weight. It stays there for the rest of the job.
steps.warn: The suspension must remain jacked throughout, to protect the ball joints.

steps.title: Free the top
steps.text: Take the covers off the top mountings in the engine bay. Adaptive damping cars: unplug the connector. Remove the mounting nuts.

steps.title: Loosen the bottom
steps.text: Remove the nut from the damper lower bolt. Leave the bolt in for now.

steps.title: Lower carefully
steps.text: Lower the jack slowly, guiding the top studs down through the body. Stop as soon as the studs clear.

steps.title: Release the upper wishbone
steps.text: Note exactly where every washer and shim sits, then remove the upper fulcrum nut and shaft. Collect the shims and move the wishbone away from the crossbeam.
steps.warn: These shims set caster. They must go back in their positions.

steps.title: Lift out
steps.text: With a helper, pull the lower bolt and take the assembly out. Do not stretch the brake hose. Temporarily put the upper wishbone back on its shaft.

steps.title: Strip and rebuild
steps.text: Fit the assembly to compressor 204-476 with the locking pin fully home. Clamp the spring, turn the handle until pressure comes off the nut, then remove and discard the damper retaining nut. Release the spring and take out the damper. Lift the gaiter out of the upper mounting and pull the spring assister from the gaiter. Assemble with the gaiter square in the upper mounting and the assister fully in the gaiter. The damper circlip must abut the lower spring pan, and the spring ends must butt against the seats. Clamp the spring, fit a new nut at 40 Nm, or 18 Nm with adaptive damping, and release it.
steps.warn: The spring is under extreme tension. Never remove the nut outside the tool, and keep your face out of line.

steps.title: Align the assembly
steps.text: Clamp the assembly in a soft-jawed vice across two of the top studs. Turn the lower bush until its bore lies parallel with two of the studs. Then it will line up in the car.

steps.title: Fit the assembly
steps.text: Release the upper wishbone. With a helper, fit the assembly and put the lower bolt through without the nut. Mind the hose.

steps.title: Refit the upper wishbone
steps.text: Refit the fulcrum shaft with the shims and washers exactly as noted. Tighten the nut to 98-132 Nm.

steps.title: Raise home
steps.text: Raise the jack and guide the studs into the body. Fit the top nuts at 26-34 Nm. Adaptive damping: line up the connector carefully, plug it in, and refit the covers.
steps.warn: A misaligned adaptive damper connector will be damaged.

steps.title: Bottom nut
steps.text: Fit the lower nut at 60-80 Nm. Lower and remove the jack.

steps.title: Refit wheels and lower
steps.text: Refit the front wheels and run the nuts up by hand. Raise off the stands, lower to the ground and torque the nuts to 88-102 Nm in a star pattern.
steps.check: Every nut clicks at 88-102 Nm.

verify: Ride height within 15 mm of spec
Wheel alignment checked, as caster shims were disturbed

diy.suits: An experienced home mechanic with the proper spring compressor. A compressed spring can kill.
diy.stop: Stop if you do not have the right compressor, or you lose track of the shims. They set the front wheel alignment.

items.title: Rear dampers and springs
items.summary: The X100 rear coil-over unit comes out through the wishbone after the hub carrier is unbolted from the wishbone and the spring is compressed on the car. Jaguar uses compressors and retaining straps. Mark the pivot pin. It sets rear toe.

parts.note: Axle pair.
British Parts lists MMD3565AA across XK8 and X308.

consumables: Grease for the upper mounting bush
safety: Never work under the car on a jack alone. Use stands on firm level ground, chock the wheels that stay down, and put the box in Park.
Many X100 nuts and bolts use thread-locking features that limit reuse. Renew any self-locking fastener that spins on easily.
Fit the compressors exactly opposite each other, with arms fully seated, and tighten them evenly. A slipping compressor is the serious risk here.
Support the hub carrier on a block. If it hangs, the handbrake cable is damaged.
Never hang the caliper on its hose.

steps.title: Raise the rear
steps.text: Box in Park, chock the front wheels. Slacken the rear wheel nuts. Put the jack centrally under the rear suspension subframe with a block of wood on the jack head and lift. Set stands at the two sill jacking points just ahead of the rear wheels, lower onto them, and take the rear wheels off.
steps.warn: Use the wood block. The jack head must not bear directly on the subframe.

steps.title: Caliper aside
steps.text: Remove the caliper spring clip, guide pin caps and pins. Lift the caliper off the carrier and tie it to the suspension bracket.

steps.title: Sensor
steps.text: Unplug the wheel speed sensor and cut the tie strap on the hose clip.

steps.title: Mark the pivot pin
steps.text: Mark the wishbone against the marker on the pivot pin eccentric flange.
steps.warn: This mark is your rear toe setting. Do not skip it.

steps.title: Free the hub carrier
steps.text: Remove the pivot pin nut and washer. Withdraw the pin, ease the carrier out and rest it on a wood block. Note the shim at each end of the pivot sleeve.
steps.warn: Shims go back in their original places.

steps.title: Compress the spring
steps.text: Fit compressors 204-179 diametrically opposite on the spring with their arms fully seated. Tighten evenly, turn by turn.
steps.warn: Check the arms after each few turns. Stop if anything shifts.

steps.title: Free the top and bottom
steps.text: Remove the damper to wishbone nut and bolt, then the nuts holding the top mounting to the body. Strap the upper mounting to the spring with 204-179-1.

steps.title: Retract the damper
steps.text: Use a jack to push the damper up through the wishbone opening, and put a bolt through the spring coils and damper lower bush to hold it short. Lower the jack part way and, on adaptive cars, press the lugs and pull the connector up.

steps.title: Take it out
steps.text: Remove the jack and lift the unit to the bench. Clean the upper spring seat. Remove the pigtail seat and clean the wishbone seat.

steps.title: Strip
steps.text: The spring stays compressed on the bench, so keep clear and leave the tools on. With help, compress the damper and draw out the temporary bolt. Hold the shaft on its flats and undo the top nut. Remove the washer, isolator, retaining straps, upper mounting, spring isolator, spring pan and packing ring. For a damper-only swap, stop here with the compressors still on the spring and go to the build-up. To change the spring, mark the tool arm positions on the spring and keep the original packers, because their type and number depend on the spring rate and some springs have none. Slacken 204-179 evenly and remove them. Transfer the marks to the new spring, fit the tools at those marks diametrically opposite, and compress it evenly.
steps.warn: A compressed spring holds a lot of energy. Slacken the compressors evenly, side to side, and never unbolt the damper from a compressed spring with your face in line.
steps.tip: On adaptive dampers the spanner goes inside the socket.

steps.title: Build up
steps.text: Fit the pigtail seat to the wishbone. Fit the spring to the upper mounting with its isolator, pan and packing ring. Strap it in the right orientation. Lightly grease the upper bush, fit it to the damper shaft, and fit the isolator, washer and locknut.

steps.title: Tighten the top nut
steps.text: Compress the damper, pop the temporary bolt in, then hold the flats and tighten the top nut to the figure below for your car. Adaptive damping has its own lower figure.

steps.title: Install
steps.text: Offer the unit up, compress the damper and take out the temporary bolt. Remove the straps. Align the lower bush and fit the bolt with its nut loose. Adaptive: connect the plug, key in keyway. Seat the upper mounting, then the pan on the studs.

steps.title: Release the spring
steps.text: Make sure the spring sits in its seat and isolator. Evenly slacken the compressors and remove them.
steps.warn: Even turns, side to side.

steps.title: Tighten mounts
steps.text: Fit the spring pan nuts at 17-23 Nm and the damper lower nut at 80-100 Nm.

steps.title: Rejoin the hub carrier
steps.text: Shims back on the sleeve in their original places. Offer up the carrier and fit the pin with its eccentric flange in the wishbone groove. Align your mark, then hold the pin and tighten the nut to the figure below for your car.

steps.title: Caliper and sensor
steps.text: Refit the caliper with guide pins at 25-30 Nm, caps and clip. Connect the speed sensor and fit a new tie strap.

steps.title: Refit wheels and lower
steps.text: Refit the rear wheels and run the nuts up by hand. Raise off the stands, lower to the ground and torque the nuts to 88-102 Nm in a star pattern.
steps.check: Every nut clicks at 88-102 Nm.

diy.suits: A specialist, or a very experienced home mechanic with the spring compressors and straps.
diy.stop: Stop if a compressor does not sit square on the spring. Have the wheel alignment checked afterwards in any case.

items.title: Exhaust flange and gaskets
items.summary: On a 4.2, each bank has two flanged joints: the catalytic converter to manifold at the top, and the converter to front silencer below. On a 4.0 only the top joint is flanged: the converter pipe slides into the front silencer and a Torca clamp holds it. Soak old nuts well in advance. Gaskets are one-use.

parts.note: One per bank if both are done.

safety: Work on a cold exhaust.
Never work under the car on a jack alone. Use stands on firm level ground, chock the wheels that stay down, and put the box in Park.
Do not jack on the aluminium front crossbeam, and do not lift the car by one front wheel. The crossbeam, steering rack and brake pipes can all be damaged.

steps.title: Raise the car
steps.text: Raise the car on stands at the sill jacking points, front high enough to work under.

steps.title: Soak the nuts
steps.text: Spray the flange nuts and clamps. Wait.

steps.title: Lower flange: drop the silencer
steps.text: Slacken the clamps behind the front silencer and pull the rear section free. 4.2: remove the flange nuts at both converters, lower the front silencer and discard both gaskets. 4.0: there are no nuts or gaskets here. Slacken the clamps at both converters and slide the silencer off the converter pipes.

steps.title: Upper flange: prepare
steps.text: Left bank: remove the coolant expansion tank. Right bank: remove the air cleaner outlet pipe. Both: unclip the catalyst monitor and oxygen sensor connectors, and note their positions. Supercharged: remove the catalyst heat shield and its bracket. On the left bank also detach the lower steering column heat shield. On the right bank also remove the EGR tube heat shield.

steps.title: Upper flange: remove the cat
steps.text: Undo the converter to manifold nuts and lift the converter away. Discard the gasket. Clean the faces.
steps.warn: Do not let the sensors take the weight.

steps.title: Refit the cat
steps.text: Fit a new gasket and hang the converter loosely, with the bracket bolts in but not tight. Lower the car if you need to reach the top nuts. Refit the shield bracket on SC cars. Tighten the nuts: 4.0 14-18 Nm, 4.2 20 Nm. Reconnect the sensors in their noted positions.
steps.warn: One video says 60-80 Nm for these nuts. That is the clamp figure, not a figure for these nuts. Do not use it here.

steps.title: Refit the silencer
steps.text: Tighten the converter bracket bolts: 4.0 39-51 Nm, 4.2 47 Nm. 4.2: fit new gaskets and the front silencer, with nuts at 47 Nm, then join the rear section and tighten the clamps to 50 Nm. 4.0: clean the joints, push the silencer onto the converter pipes and then onto the rear section, and set each joint between its marks. Tighten the rear clamps, then the converter clamps, to 60-80 Nm.
steps.tip: Jaguar's 4.0 figures for the clamps disagree: 60-80 Nm in the exhaust section, 50-60 Nm in the engine section. Only 60 Nm fits both. This is not resolved.

verify: No blow at any exhaust joint on a cold start

diy.suits: Someone with stands and patience. Old exhaust fixings are often stuck fast.
diy.stop: Stop if a stud or nut will not move, or breaks. Heating and drilling them out is a garage job.

items.title: Starter motor
items.summary: Fits from below, tight against the steering rack. The upper bolt is the whole story. A short 13 mm spanner or a half-moon spanner starts it, then a socket with universal joint and extensions. JTIS MY2000 takes the power steering rack out from below for access, then refills and bleeds the steering. LHD owners have done it without that, which is unverified, especially on RHD.
consumables: Power steering fluid if the rack comes out
safety: Disconnect the battery ground first. The heavy starter cable is always live.
Never work under the car on a jack alone. Use stands on firm level ground, chock the wheels that stay down, and put the box in Park.
Do not jack on the aluminium front crossbeam, and do not lift the car by one front wheel. The crossbeam, steering rack and brake pipes can all be damaged.
The car needs to be well up for working room. Double check the stands before you get under.
The starter is heavy and comes out at awkward angles. Keep your face clear.

steps.title: Doors open, battery off
steps.text: Open the driver's door, or both doors, so the frameless glass drops. Keep the doors open until the battery is disconnected. Then disconnect the battery ground in the boot.
steps.warn: With the glass still up and the battery off, shutting a door can foul the seal or the hood rail.

steps.title: Raise high
steps.text: Jack centrally, on a wood or rubber pad, under the front body crossmember, which is the steel lower crossmember right at the front of the car, the one the towing eye screws into, not the aluminium suspension crossbeam behind it, and set stands at the sill jacking points as high as they will safely go.
steps.warn: Never jack on the aluminium crossbeam.

steps.title: Clear the duct
steps.text: Remove the plastic oil filter cover and the alternator cooling air tube. This lets you line up the extensions.

steps.title: Disconnect the cables
steps.text: Move the starter cable cover aside and undo both cables.

steps.title: Upper bolt
steps.text: Crack the upper bolt with a short 13 mm spanner or a Snap-on half-moon spanner CMX1113. Then spin it out with a 3/8 inch drive 13 mm socket, a universal joint and extensions. An LHD owner had about 3.5 cm of room between the heat shield and the tunnel.
steps.warn: On RHD the steering input shaft may limit access further. One UK owner was hoping to slide the starter forward with the filter and spigot off.

steps.title: Lower bolt
steps.text: Remove the lower bolt.

steps.title: Extract it
steps.text: Factory route: remove the power steering rack from below first, then lift the starter out. Owner shortcut, unverified: ease the starter out past the rack without removing it. LHD owners report that it goes without lifting the engine. RHD access is unconfirmed.

steps.title: Fit the new starter
steps.text: Offer it up, start both bolts by hand, and tighten. 4.0: 38-48 Nm. 4.2: 45 Nm in the manual, and the spec book says 43 Nm.

steps.title: Cables
steps.text: Refit the battery cable and the solenoid cable. 4.2: 10 Nm and 7 Nm. No figure sourced for the 4.0. Refit the cover.

steps.title: Finish
steps.text: Refit the duct and, if it came out, refit the rack, refill the reservoir with the specified fluid and bleed the steering. Lower the car.

steps.title: Reconnect and relearn
steps.text: Leave the battery off for at least 30 seconds in all, then reconnect the ground cable with one clean, firm contact and tighten to 4 Nm. Ignition on. Reset each window: hold the switch down for 5 seconds past the bottom stop, then up for 5 seconds past the top stop. Re-enter the radio code and set the clock. Let the engine computer relearn: idle to full temperature, switch off, restart and idle for 2 minutes, hold 2 minutes in Drive on the brake, then drive about 5 miles of varied roads.

verify: Clean crank, no click or whine
Cable nuts tight with no heat at the terminals

diy.suits: An experienced home mechanic. The upper bolt is very hard to reach, and the car must be well up on stands.
diy.stop: Stop if you cannot reach the upper bolt, or the car is not high enough to work under safely.

items.title: Front wheel bearing
items.summary: A sealed cartridge pressed into the vertical link. Hub removal destroys it, so never reuse one. The job needs a press, and the hub rotor nut is a very high 270 to 330 Nm. Maximum end float is 0.13 mm.

parts.note: Always new once the hub comes out.
Discard the old ones.
Needed on cars before VIN 018108.
Always new.

safety: Never work under the car on a jack alone. Use stands on firm level ground, chock the wheels that stay down, and put the box in Park.
Do not jack on the aluminium front crossbeam, and do not lift the car by one front wheel. The crossbeam, steering rack and brake pipes can all be damaged.
Many X100 nuts and bolts use thread-locking features that limit reuse. Renew any self-locking fastener that spins on easily.
Do not let the vertical link hang on a ball joint.
Press work: wear eye protection and stay out of the line of a slipping part.
Never hang the caliper on its hose.

steps.title: Raise the front
steps.text: Handbrake on, box in Park, chock the rear wheels. Slacken the front wheel nuts. Put the trolley jack, with a wood or rubber pad on its head, centrally under the front body crossmember and lift. That is the steel lower crossmember right at the front of the car, the one the towing eye screws into, not the aluminium suspension crossbeam behind it. Set stands at the two sill jacking points just behind the front wheels, lower onto them, and take the front wheels off.
steps.warn: Jack on the body crossmember, never on the aluminium suspension crossbeam. The Vehicle Care book says not to use jacking equipment under the front cross member, without saying which one. Jaguar's workshop text puts the jack on the body crossmember and forbids the aluminium suspension crossbeam, so that is the one to keep off. No photo confirms this reading: if you cannot tell them apart, stop and read the Jacking page.

steps.title: Diagnose first
steps.text: A rumble or end float over 0.13 mm confirms a bad bearing. Do not confuse ball joint or bush movement with bearing play. A little grease at the seal is normal.

steps.title: Remove disc
steps.text: Remove the caliper and disc as in the disc job. Tie the caliper up.

steps.title: Speed sensor
steps.text: Remove the wheel speed sensor bolt and ease out the sensor. Cut the harness ties and move the harness clear.

steps.title: Tie rod end
steps.text: Remove the tie rod end nut, fit taper separator 211-098 and tighten its bolt until the taper lets go.

steps.title: Upper ball joint
steps.text: Remove the upper ball joint nut. Use separator 204-192 to release the taper.
steps.warn: Do not use 211-098 on ball joints. It tears the gaiter.

steps.title: Lower ball joint
steps.text: Remove the lower ball joint nut. Use splitter 204-293 to release it and lift the vertical link and hub off the car.
steps.warn: Do not let the link hang on the lower joint.

steps.title: Strip the hub
steps.text: Remove the disc shield screws and shield. Clamp holding tool 204-195 in a vice and fix the hub to it with wheel nuts. Remove the rotor nut spring clip and undo the rotor nut with socket 206-066A.

steps.title: Press out the hub
steps.text: Stand the link in collets 204-194 on the press with a shield screw boss in the middle of one collet. Put remover 204-193 on the hub and press it out.
steps.warn: This ruins the bearing. Never refit it.

steps.title: Press out the bearing
steps.text: Remove and discard both circlips. Support the inboard side of the bore level on the press, close to the bore. Press out with tool 204-197. Clean the link.

steps.title: Fit the bearing
steps.text: Fit the outboard circlip with the ear gap at the lowest point in the car. Press in the new bearing using 204-198, seating with a 3 ton load. Fit the inboard circlip the same way, using plier tips that do not poke past the ears into the seal.
steps.warn: The circlip gap must sit at the bottom so water drains out.
steps.tip: One owner's write-up says 6 tons according to Jaguar. Every JTIS year and the 2003-06 manual say 3 tons.

steps.title: Fit the hub
steps.text: Stand the link inboard face down on tool 204-196. Lay a flat steel plate across the hub, clear of the studs. Press with a 3 ton seating load.
steps.warn: Do not press on the wheel studs.

steps.title: Fit the rotor nut
steps.text: Back in the holding tool. Cars before VIN 018108 must get a grease deflector, set at 0.5 mm. Tighten the rotor nut to 270-330 Nm with socket 206-066A. Fit a new spring clip through the hub holes and nut slots. If the slots do not line up, tighten more. Never slacken it.
steps.tip: The earlier socket 206-066 is limited to 190 Nm. From XKR VIN A41332 the 206-066A tool must be shortened by 13 mm to fit.

steps.title: Back on the car
steps.text: Fit the shield. Fit the vertical link to the car. Upper and lower ball joint nuts 60-80 Nm. Tie rod end nut 71-85 Nm. Refit the speed sensor bolt.

steps.title: Brakes
steps.text: Refit the disc, the carrier with its bolts at the figure below for your car, then the pads and caliper with guide pins at 25-30 Nm.

steps.title: Refit wheels and lower
steps.text: Refit the front wheels and run the nuts up by hand. Raise off the stands, lower to the ground and torque the nuts to 88-102 Nm in a star pattern.
steps.check: Every nut clicks at 88-102 Nm.

diy.suits: A specialist, or a home mechanic with a workshop press and the Jaguar tools.
diy.stop: Stop before you begin if you have no press. The bearing cannot be changed without one, and the hub nut is very tight.

items.title: Rear wheel bearing
items.summary: Unlike the front, the rear uses two taper bearings set with a selective shim to 0.076 mm end float. It needs a press, a dial gauge and a hub puller. Expect a long day or more and a real workshop. Fit a new hub nut: the Axle Shaft procedure says so, the Wheel Bearing procedure does not, so follow the stricter one.

parts.note: Inner and outer, with cups.
Selected on assembly.
Always new. JTIS Axle Shaft says do not reuse the original nut.

safety: Never work under the car on a jack alone. Use stands on firm level ground, chock the wheels that stay down, and put the box in Park.
Brake dust is a health risk. Remove it with a vacuum brush, not an air line.
Many X100 nuts and bolts use thread-locking features that limit reuse. Renew any self-locking fastener that spins on easily.
The hub nut is 304-336 Nm, so plan your torque wrench and holding tool.
A hub puller stores a lot of energy. Release it with care and keep your face out of line.
Do not press on wheel studs.

steps.title: Raise the rear
steps.text: Box in Park, chock the front wheels. Slacken the rear wheel nuts. Put the jack centrally under the rear suspension subframe with a block of wood on the jack head and lift. Set stands at the two sill jacking points just ahead of the rear wheels, lower onto them, and take the rear wheels off. Jaguar reaches the cable first on a lift. At home, do the next step from underneath once the car is on stands.
steps.warn: Use the wood block. The jack head must not bear directly on the subframe.

steps.title: Slacken the handbrake cable
steps.text: Release the handbrake. Fully slacken but do not remove the cable adjuster nut. Free the cable on that side from its connecting clip. Left cable: draw it through the equaliser.

steps.title: Crack the hub nut
steps.text: Bolt holding tool 204-195 to the wheel studs and slacken but do not remove the hub nut. Take the tool off.

steps.title: Strip the brake
steps.text: Remove the rear disc and handbrake shoes as in the rear disc job and the handbrake shoe procedure. Remove the speed sensor.

steps.title: Pull the hub
steps.text: Remove and discard the hub nut, then the locating collar. Fit a thread protector to the axle shaft. Fix puller 204-011 to the studs with the wheel nuts and tighten the centre bolt progressively.
steps.warn: The hub can release suddenly under load. Tighten progressively and keep your face out of line.

steps.title: Backplate
steps.text: Release the handbrake cable from the suspension bracket and carrier grommet. Remove the backplate with the cable attached.

steps.title: Remove the carrier
steps.text: Mark and remove the pivot pin nut and washer. Withdraw the pin and take off the hub and carrier. Note the shim at each end of the sleeve, and withdraw the sleeve.
steps.warn: Pivot shims go back in the same places.

steps.title: Press out and strip
steps.text: Use 204-113 on the press with the handbrake cable housing in the recess and press the hub out. Remove the ABS rotor. Drift out seals, bearings, spacer and shim. Drift out both cups, then clean everything.

steps.title: Fit the cups
steps.text: Press in the inner and outer cups with handle 100-013 and the 204-118 adaptors.

steps.title: Trial build
steps.text: Fit the outer bearing and hub dry. Fit the spacer, a 3.47 mm maximum shim and the inner bearing. Press on the ABS rotor with the carrier on a wood block. Never load the studs.

steps.title: Measure end float
steps.text: Clamp the carrier in a vice. Fit spacer tool JD15 and dial gauge JD 13A. Lever gently with two levers and record end float.
steps.warn: Do not use excessive force when levering.

steps.title: Choose the shim
steps.text: Press everything apart. From the measured figure, choose the shim that gives 0.076 mm end float.
steps.check: Target is 0.076 mm.

steps.title: Final build
steps.text: Pack both new bearings with Retinax A. Fit the outer bearing and seat its seal with 205-234. Press in the hub. Fit the spacer, the chosen shim and inner bearing, seat the inner seal with 205-234. Press on the ABS rotor.

steps.title: Rejoin the car
steps.text: Fit the pivot sleeve and shims. Offer the hub and carrier to the wishbone and axle shaft. Fit the pin with its thread forward, and leave the nut loose. Route the cable and fit its grommet. Clean old locking agent off the hub splines, put Loctite 270 on the shaft splines and thread and seat the hub.

steps.title: Tighten in order
steps.text: Fit the collar and a new hub nut, loose. Tighten the pivot pin nut to the figure below for your car. Fit the speed sensor at 8-10 Nm with a new tie strap. Refit shoes and disc. With holding tool 204-195 on, tighten the hub nut to 304-336 Nm.

steps.title: Refit wheels and lower
steps.text: Refit the rear wheels and run the nuts up by hand. Raise off the stands, lower to the ground and torque the nuts to 88-102 Nm in a star pattern.
steps.check: Every nut clicks at 88-102 Nm.

steps.title: Handbrake and alignment
steps.text: Route the cable back through the bracket and equaliser. Adjust so the lever applies in 3 to 5 clicks with the rear wheels spinning free when released. Check rear toe.

diy.suits: A specialist, or a home mechanic with a workshop press and the Jaguar tools.
diy.stop: Stop before you begin if you have no press, dial gauge and hub puller. The bearing has to be set up exactly.

items.title: Front lower ball joint and rear lower arm
items.summary: The manual treats the lower ball joint and rear lower arm as one assembly. The lower wishbone comes off, is split into its two arms, and a new rear arm is built up with its bush. The spec table also lists a 25 to 50 kN press-in load for the joint, but the procedure swaps the arm. PistonHeads notes the lower mounts wear and need the arm off, so inspect the bushes now.

parts.note: Includes the lower ball joint.

safety: Never work under the car on a jack alone. Use stands on firm level ground, chock the wheels that stay down, and put the box in Park.
Do not jack on the aluminium front crossbeam, and do not lift the car by one front wheel. The crossbeam, steering rack and brake pipes can all be damaged.
Many X100 nuts and bolts use thread-locking features that limit reuse. Renew any self-locking fastener that spins on easily.
Wire the vertical link to the road spring before freeing the ball joint, to protect the upper joint.

steps.title: Raise the front
steps.text: Handbrake on, box in Park, chock the rear wheels. Slacken the front wheel nuts. Put the trolley jack, with a wood or rubber pad on its head, centrally under the front body crossmember and lift. That is the steel lower crossmember right at the front of the car, the one the towing eye screws into, not the aluminium suspension crossbeam behind it. Set stands at the two sill jacking points just behind the front wheels, lower onto them, and take the front wheels off.
steps.warn: Jack on the body crossmember, never on the aluminium suspension crossbeam. The Vehicle Care book says not to use jacking equipment under the front cross member, without saying which one. Jaguar's workshop text puts the jack on the body crossmember and forbids the aluminium suspension crossbeam, so that is the one to keep off. No photo confirms this reading: if you cannot tell them apart, stop and read the Jacking page.

steps.title: Free the link
steps.text: Remove the nut and bolt holding the anti-roll link to the lower wishbone.

steps.title: Wire up the link
steps.text: Tie the vertical link to the road spring with strong wire.

steps.title: Split the ball joint
steps.text: Remove the ball joint nut. Fit splitter 204-293, make sure the gaiter is not trapped, and tighten until the taper lets go.
steps.warn: Do not use tool 211-098 here. It damages the gaiter.

steps.title: Remove the wishbone
steps.text: Remove the damper lower nut and bolt, then the front and rear arm fulcrum nuts and bolts. Note and mark which fulcrum bolt is which: some cars have an eccentric bolt on the rear arm, and every bolt must go back in its original position. Lift the wishbone away.
steps.warn: A swapped eccentric bolt changes the wheel alignment.

steps.title: Split the arms
steps.text: Clamp the front arm in a vice. Remove the two bolts joining the arms. Discard the rear arm and ball joint assembly. Keep the damper brackets. Clean up the front arm and brackets.

steps.title: Press in the bush
steps.text: Stand the new rear arm on the press, front end up. Put the bush on it and a steel plate on top. Allow clearance beneath for the bush to stand proud, and press it home.

steps.title: Build the wishbone
steps.text: Put the damper brackets and bolts on the rear arm and fit the front arm. Fit the link bolt and nut loosely to line up the damper brackets while you tighten the two joining bolts to 128-172 Nm, then take the link bolt out. Remove the plastic transit cover from the new ball joint.

steps.title: Refit the wishbone
steps.text: Offer it to the crossbeam and fit the rear and front fulcrum bolts, not tightened yet. Fit the ball joint nut at 60-80 Nm.

steps.title: Damper and fulcrums
steps.text: Fit the damper lower bolt at 60-80 Nm. Remove the wire. Tighten the rear fulcrum to 113-153 Nm, then the front fulcrum the same.

steps.title: Link
steps.text: Refit the anti-roll link at 39-55 Nm.

steps.title: Refit wheels and lower
steps.text: Refit the front wheels and run the nuts up by hand. Raise off the stands, lower to the ground and torque the nuts to 88-102 Nm in a star pattern.
steps.check: Every nut clicks at 88-102 Nm.

diy.suits: An experienced home mechanic with a ball joint splitter and the use of a press.
diy.stop: Stop if the joint will not split with the right tool. Have the wheel alignment checked afterwards.

items.title: Radiator
items.summary: A bigger job than it looks, because the condenser pipes and gearbox cooler lines all connect here. The air conditioning must be recovered before the pipes are undone, and that needs a licensed recovery machine.

parts.note: New O-rings on every gearbox and A/C joint.

consumables: New foam sealing strips for the radiator, 4.0
safety: Open the expansion tank cap only when the engine has cooled. Wrap it in a thick cloth, turn slowly, and step back while pressure escapes.
The cooling fan can start with the engine off when hot. Pull fuse 14 in the engine management fuse box before working near it, and refit it before starting.
Never work under the car on a jack alone. Use stands on firm level ground, chock the wheels that stay down, and put the box in Park.
Do not jack on the aluminium front crossbeam, and do not lift the car by one front wheel. The crossbeam, steering rack and brake pipes can all be damaged.
Do not vent refrigerant. Recovery and recharge are specialist work.

steps.title: Recover the A/C
steps.text: Have the air conditioning recovered by someone with the kit.
steps.warn: Do this before touching any A/C pipe.

steps.title: Doors open, battery off
steps.text: Open the driver's door, or both doors, so the frameless glass drops. Keep the doors open until the battery is disconnected. Then disconnect the battery ground cable in the boot.
steps.warn: With the glass still up and the battery off, shutting a door can foul the seal or the hood rail.

steps.title: Drain and raise
steps.text: Drain the coolant as in the coolant job. Keep the front raised safely on stands at the sill jacking points.

steps.title: Fan and hoses off
steps.text: Remove the air cleaner. Detach the A/C tube. Lower the car. Remove the radiator top and bottom hoses, on supercharged cars also the intercooler hose and vent hose. Detach the wiring harness. Remove the fan shroud retaining bolt and unplug the fan connectors. Lift the fan motor and shroud out. 4.0: the fan plugs are reached from under the car, and Jaguar lifts the cowl out still on the radiator, then parts them on the bench.

steps.title: Top panel, 4.0
steps.text: Remove the five bolts holding the radiator top panel, then the panel and the top mounting rubbers.

steps.title: A/C pipes
steps.text: Undo the A/C pipe nuts and the receiver drier to condenser pipe. Discard the O-rings and cap every port straight away.

steps.title: Gearbox lines
steps.text: Disconnect the lower and upper gearbox cooler pipes. Discard the O-rings and cap the ports. Expect some ATF.

steps.title: Supercharged extras
steps.text: Also disconnect the radiator vent hose.

steps.title: Cross brace
steps.text: Convertibles: remove the radiator grille opening cross brace.

steps.title: Lift it out
steps.text: Remove the radiator support bracket and condenser pipe protection bracket. Undo the retaining bolts and, with a helper, lift the radiator out.

steps.title: Fit the new radiator
steps.text: Fit the radiator, pipe bracket and retaining brackets. 4.2: 10 Nm. No figure sourced for the 4.0. 4.0: fit new foam strips to the top, bottom and left side of the radiator first, sit it on its lower rubbers with a helper, and fit the top panel with its five bolts. Refit the cross brace on convertibles.

steps.title: Rejoin the pipes
steps.text: Uncap and fit new O-rings. Gearbox cooler pipes at the radiator: 20 Nm on a 4.2 and on an XKR 4.0 from MY2000. JTIS prints no figure for other 4.0 cars. Receiver drier pipe 10 Nm. A/C pipes 10 Nm. Clean any oil residue.

steps.title: Finish
steps.text: Refit the fan, refill and bleed the coolant, and have the A/C evacuated and recharged. Check and reset the gearbox fluid level.

steps.title: Reconnect and relearn
steps.text: Leave the battery off for at least 30 seconds in all, then reconnect the ground cable with one clean, firm contact and tighten to 4 Nm. Ignition on. Reset each window: hold the switch down for 5 seconds past the bottom stop, then up for 5 seconds past the top stop. Re-enter the radio code and set the clock. Let the engine computer relearn: idle to full temperature, switch off, restart and idle for 2 minutes, hold 2 minutes in Drive on the brake, then drive about 5 miles of varied roads.

diy.suits: An experienced home mechanic, with a specialist booked to recover the air conditioning first.
diy.stop: Stop before any air conditioning pipe is undone. The refrigerant must be recovered by a specialist first.

items.title: Propshaft and flexible coupling
items.summary: The propshaft has a flexible coupling at the gearbox, a centre bearing and a bolted flange at the diff. Jaguar's manual treats the coupling as staying on the shaft and warns not to undo it from the shaft. Owners have replaced cracked couplings regardless. 1998 NA has a one-piece shaft, later cars a two-piece.

parts.note: If the shaft or bearing is worn.
Forum sources disagree on whether Jaguar lists this as serviceable.

safety: Never work under the car on a jack alone. Use stands on firm level ground, chock the wheels that stay down, and put the box in Park.
Support the shaft once it is free. A dropped tube is out of balance for good.
Mark everything. Bolts and flange positions all go back as they came, to keep the balance. Nuts are new nylon-insert nuts.

steps.title: Raise the car
steps.text: Raise the car on four stands at the sill jacking points, box in Neutral and handbrake off once secure.

steps.title: Exhaust out of the way
steps.text: Remove the front silencer as in the exhaust job.

steps.title: Handbrake linkage
steps.text: Remove the handbrake cable adjuster nut and cable retaining bracket, and detach the front cable.

steps.title: Centre bearing
steps.text: Detach the propshaft centre bearing. Remove the handbrake lever and centre bearing mounting plate.

steps.title: Mark the joints
steps.text: Mark the shaft against the gearbox flange. Mark each nut and bolt against the flexible joint.
steps.warn: The manual says the coupling and its fixings must never be loosened or removed from the shaft.

steps.title: Unbolt and remove
steps.text: Undo the fixings at the gearbox flange and at the rear axle flange and lower the shaft out.

steps.title: Coupling only, 1998 one-piece
steps.text: One owner's method: remove the six bolts, separate the two rear silencers from the centre silencer, lower the centre silencer, remove the handbrake relay shroud and let the front of the shaft drop enough to free the coupling. Another found the rear joint had to be undone as well.
steps.warn: Check the moulded direction arrows on the coupling before you remove the old one.

steps.title: Refit the shaft
steps.text: Offer up the shaft and match your marks. Fit new nylon-insert nuts; bolts can be reused if undamaged. 4.2: rear flange bolts 60 Nm, gearbox flange nuts and bolts 88 Nm, centre bearing bolts 25 Nm. 4.0: rear flange 51-69 Nm, production figure 60 Nm, with Loctite 270 on the bolt threads; flexible coupling 75-88 Nm, production figure 78 Nm.

steps.title: Rebuild
steps.text: Refit the mounting plate, lever and cable. Adjust the handbrake so it applies in 3 to 5 clicks. Refit the silencer as in the exhaust job: new gaskets on a 4.2, clamps only on a 4.0.

verify: No vibration at any road speed

diy.suits: An experienced home mechanic. Jaguar's own manual says not to disturb the coupling.
diy.stop: Stop if you have not marked everything. The shaft must go back as it came to stay in balance. A vibration afterwards needs a specialist.

items.title: Vee mounts (front crossbeam rear mounts)
items.summary: Vendors use the name vee mount for the rubber mount at the rear of the front subframe. The X100 manual calls these crossbeam rear mountings. Jaguar has no job for the mount alone. This follows one owner's 2006 write-up of lowering only the rear of the crossbeam on a jack, with torques from the factory crossbeam job. It is one owner's method at his own risk, not a factory job. Another owner warns that the centre Torx bolt rounds off, and then the whole crossbeam has to come down.

parts.note: SNG Barratt's XK8 catalogue lists MJA2360AH, qty 2. Check by VIN.

safety: Never work under the car on a jack alone. Use stands on firm level ground, chock the wheels that stay down, and put the box in Park.
Do not jack on the aluminium front crossbeam, and do not lift the car by one front wheel. The crossbeam, steering rack and brake pipes can all be damaged.
Support the engine and the crossbeam before any mount bolt comes out.
Support the crossbeam on a jack with a wood block. Bare steel on the casting will damage it.
Many X100 nuts and bolts use thread-locking features that limit reuse. Renew any self-locking fastener that spins on easily.

steps.title: Support the engine
steps.text: Open the driver's door, or both doors, so the frameless glass drops. Keep the doors open until the battery is disconnected. Then disconnect the battery ground and remove the engine covers. The manual supports the engine from above: fit the beam 303-021 across the wing channels, hook into the front lifting eyes and take up the weight.
steps.warn: The factory job supports the engine because it also frees the front engine mounts. The owner's write-up mentions neither. Supporting it here is the cautious choice.

steps.title: Raise and strip
steps.text: Raise the front as in the front raising step and take off the front wheels. Remove the alternator front cooling duct. Remove the undertray, discarding its eight scrivets. Convertibles: remove the cruciform strut.

steps.title: Support the crossbeam
steps.text: Put a jack with a wood block under the crossbeam and take the weight.
steps.warn: Wood block between jack and crossbeam.

steps.title: Release the rear mounting
steps.text: Undo the four 13 mm steering rack bolts and support the rack so it does not hang on its pipes. Undo the front and rear lower wishbone bolts on both sides, 21 mm and 18 mm in the owner's account, and swing each wishbone clear of the small mount bolts. With the jack still under the beam, undo the centre T55 bolt and the four T40 bolts on each side. Do both sides before lowering: the owner needed both undone to lever the new mount onto its peg. Jaguar's own sequence instead frees the dampers, anti-roll links, engine mounts and front brackets, and the owner's account mentions none of those.
steps.warn: Keep the jack under the beam at all times. If the centre bolt head starts to round off, stop: one owner says the whole crossbeam then has to come down to reach it.

steps.title: Lower a little
steps.text: Lower the rear of the crossbeam gently on the jack until the mounts just clear. Bring the jack back up until it only just holds the beam, and lock it so nothing drops unnoticed. Watch the brake pipes, steering and wiring as it moves. The owner found the beam stopped dropping on its own after a short way, but do not rely on that.
steps.warn: Check every pipe and loom for slack before lowering further.

steps.title: Swap the mount
steps.text: Lift out the old mount. It may come apart, and its centre can corrode onto the tapered body peg and need levering off. Lever the new mount onto the peg, between the beam and the body. Fit the centre bolt and the four T40 bolts loosely on each side so the beam lines itself up.

steps.title: Raise and secure
steps.text: Jack the crossbeam back up gently, and stop before it starts to lift the car off its stands: the beam is not made to carry the car. Tighten the centre bolt to the body at 77-103 Nm and the four mount to crossbeam bolts at 26-34 Nm. Repeat for the other side.

steps.title: Rebuild
steps.text: Refit the lower wishbone bolts and tighten each to 113-153 Nm, rear then front. Refit the rack bolts to the figure below. If the front brackets were released, fit them at 77-103 Nm, starting the front bolts loose, tightening the rear bolt, then the front ones. Remove the jack. Refit the strut, undertray, duct, engine support and covers. Refit the front wheels, lower to the ground and torque the nuts to 88-102 Nm.

steps.title: Reconnect and relearn
steps.text: Leave the battery off for at least 30 seconds in all, then reconnect the ground cable with one clean, firm contact and tighten to 4 Nm. Ignition on. Reset each window: hold the switch down for 5 seconds past the bottom stop, then up for 5 seconds past the top stop. Re-enter the radio code and set the clock. Let the engine computer relearn: idle to full temperature, switch off, restart and idle for 2 minutes, hold 2 minutes in Drive on the brake, then drive about 5 miles of varied roads.

diy.suits: An experienced home mechanic with an engine support beam. Jaguar has no procedure for this mount alone.
diy.stop: Stop if you cannot support the engine and the crossbeam properly. Check the part fits your car before you start.

items.title: Supercharger coupler
items.summary: A rattle at idle can be the coupler, a small part inside the supercharger nose. Jaguar has no procedure. The factory line was to swap the whole supercharger, so this is owner knowledge. On the X100 the unit comes off first, and the nose is opened on the bench. Inspect the rear bearings and rotors at the same time.

parts.note: Powerhouse lists an OEM-style Eaton sprung coupler for XKR 4.0 and 4.2 from 1998 to 2005.
Owners renew these plastic pipes while the unit is off.

consumables: Supercharger nose oil, the correct grade
Silicone sealant for the nose joint
safety: Open the expansion tank cap only when the engine has cooled. Wrap it in a thick cloth, turn slowly, and step back while pressure escapes.
The cooling fan can start with the engine off when hot. Pull fuse 14 in the engine management fuse box before working near it, and refit it before starting.
Open a door so the glass drops, then disconnect the battery ground.
Keep all dirt out of the intake and rotor pack.
Do not drive with a loud rattle for long. Powerhouse warns the rotors can start to eat themselves and the casing.

steps.title: Diagnose
steps.text: Listen with a stethoscope. Rattle at idle, or a shudder and clonk at switch-off, points to the coupler. Noise that goes as the idle rises is typical. Do not assume: on a 2003 4.2 the noise came from the rotors.
steps.tip: Later 4.2 rotors have a Teflon coating, which is not carbon. Leave it.

steps.title: Doors open, battery off
steps.text: Open the driver's door, or both doors, so the frameless glass drops. Keep the doors open until the battery is disconnected. Then disconnect the battery ground cable in the boot.
steps.warn: With the glass still up and the battery off, shutting a door can foul the seal or the hood rail.

steps.title: Drain and strip
steps.text: Drain the cooling system. Remove the throttle body, EGR tube and supercharger outlet pipe. Detach and move the engine harness.

steps.title: Disconnect
steps.text: Disconnect the booster vacuum hose, breather, EGR to heater hose, purge tube, EGR valve and MAP sensor connectors.

steps.title: Remove the elbow
steps.text: Remove both elbow bolts, move the charge air cooler hose clips and take off the throttle elbow. Discard the gasket and bolt seals.

steps.title: Belt off
steps.text: Disconnect the right fan plug and take the supercharger belt off with tool 303-631.

steps.title: Thermostat housing
steps.text: Disconnect the radiator to housing hoses, expansion tank hose, and temperature sensor. Detach the thermostat housing and its heater hose. Discard the seals.

steps.title: Lift the supercharger
steps.text: Disconnect the charge air cooler to pump hose. Move the harness from the bracket and left valve cover. Lift off the supercharger.

steps.title: Open the nose on the bench
steps.text: Drain the nose oil into a pan. Undo the nose bolts. Release the joint with a soft mallet or by careful levering at a proper point. Protect the sealing faces.
steps.warn: Bolt count and torque for the Jaguar nose were not found. Later engine write-ups do not transfer directly.

steps.title: Swap the coupler
steps.text: Pull off the old coupler. Fit the new one to the pins. It is meant to be a tight fit, so do not rush to file it. One owner on a different engine did have to ease the holes.
steps.check: Check the rotor shaft for play and the rear bearings for roughness. Worn bearings can let the rotors touch the case.

steps.title: Close the nose
steps.text: Clean all old sealant off. Run a thin bead of silicone, close the nose and tighten evenly. Fill with the correct oil.

steps.title: Refit the supercharger
steps.text: Clean the seat. Align the spacer plate to the block before lowering the unit. Bolts are 24 Nm in the intake section table. The engine table says 20 Nm, and the spec book says 21 Nm.
steps.warn: Check the spacer plate alignment first. Guide pins made from M8 threaded rod help hold the gaskets.

steps.title: Rebuild
steps.text: Thermostat housing with new seals: 4.2 10 Nm. JTIS prints no housing figure for the 4.0, only 8-10 Nm for the cover. Belt on. Elbow with new gasket and seals (4.2: 24 Nm. No figure sourced for the 4.0.) Reconnect all hoses and plugs. Refit outlet pipe and EGR tube. Refit the throttle body.

steps.title: Reconnect and relearn
steps.text: Reconnect before the refill, because the supercharger fill needs the ignition on. Leave the battery off for at least 30 seconds in all, then reconnect the ground cable with one clean, firm contact and tighten to 4 Nm. Ignition on. Reset each window: hold the switch down for 5 seconds past the bottom stop, then up for 5 seconds past the top stop. Re-enter the radio code and set the clock. Let the engine computer relearn: idle to full temperature, switch off, restart and idle for 2 minutes, hold 2 minutes in Drive on the brake, then drive about 5 miles of varied roads.

steps.title: Refill and test
steps.text: Refill and bleed coolant, including the supercharger port. Start and listen.

verify: No oil at the nose joint

diy.suits: A specialist or a supercharger rebuilder. Jaguar has no procedure for this.
diy.stop: Stop before you open the nose of the supercharger. The bolt tightness and sealant are not known, so ask a rebuilder first.

items.title: Valley hoses
items.summary: On 1997-99 naturally aspirated cars, VIN 010343-042635 in Jaguar's bulletin, two heater hoses run in the valley under the intake manifold and fracture at the block end. XKRs have a coolant pipe through the V instead, which means a much bigger strip. The intake has to come off, and the job needs a day. While it is off, renew the octopus hose, coolant pipes, gaskets and knock sensor leads.

parts.note: NNE3946CA on a 1999 XK8. Verify by VIN.
NCA3945CD on a 1999 XK8. Verify by VIN.
NNE3944BA.
MJA6728AC. Verify by VIN.

consumables: Length of fuel hose for odd vacuum lines
safety: Fuel stays under pressure long after switch-off. Release it first, work outdoors or well ventilated, keep sparks and phones away, and have a catch pan ready.
Open the expansion tank cap only when the engine has cooled. Wrap it in a thick cloth, turn slowly, and step back while pressure escapes.
The cooling fan can start with the engine off when hot. Pull fuse 14 in the engine management fuse box before working near it, and refit it before starting.
Stuff the intake ports with clean rag once the manifold is off.
Take photos of every connection.

steps.title: Prepare
steps.text: Open the driver's door, or both doors, so the frameless glass drops. Keep the doors open until the battery is disconnected. Then disconnect the battery ground. Release the fuel pressure. With the engine cold, release the cooling system pressure at the expansion tank cap, then drain the cooling system. Remove the air cleaner outlet pipe.
steps.warn: With the glass still up and the battery off, shutting a door can foul the seal or the hood rail.

steps.title: Unload the top
steps.text: Remove the engine cover brackets, detach the knock sensor connectors and engine harness. Disconnect the hoses and pipes at the rear.

steps.title: Electrical
steps.text: Unplug the EGR valve, fuel temperature sensor, right camshaft sensor, fuel pressure regulator, throttle body and MAP sensor. Move the harness clear.

steps.title: Coolant and vacuum
steps.text: Take the coolant hose off the expansion tank and the throttle body coolant hoses. Disconnect the vacuum hose.

steps.title: EGR tube
steps.text: Remove the EGR tube heat shield nut and shield, then the tube bolts. Discard the gasket.

steps.title: Lift the manifold
steps.text: Disconnect the fuel lines at the rail. Lift off the manifold with the throttle body attached. The elbow can stay attached to the manifold. Discard the gaskets and block the ports.
steps.warn: An XJ8 owner took eight hours to get this far.

steps.title: Supercharged cars
steps.text: The route to the valley is via the supercharger removal job. See the supercharger coupler job for that sequence.

steps.title: Change the hoses
steps.text: Lift out the foam block. Remove both valley hoses and the tee. The left hose runs from the tee off the octopus hose to its block connection under the rear of the thermostat tower, and that is where they tend to fracture. Fit the new hoses in the grooves of the foam.
steps.tip: A Norma quick connector is at the rear. Slide the outer ring away from the pipe to release it. One owner had to cut a frozen one off.

steps.title: Do the neighbours
steps.text: While you are here, renew the octopus hose, the three heater hoses, any vacuum line under the manifold, and consider both knock sensors and the small hose off the rear of the valley hose. Inspect the thermostat housing and its rear bolts.

steps.title: Clean
steps.text: Clean out the valley. Clean the gasket faces without letting debris into the ports.

steps.title: Refit the manifold
steps.text: Remove the rags. Fit new gaskets and bolt the manifold down at 22 Nm.
steps.warn: The 4.2 manual says 22 Nm and the V8 page of the spec book says 21 Nm.

steps.title: Rebuild
steps.text: Refit the EGR tube with a new gasket, and on the 4.2 the heat shield nut at 20 Nm. EGR tube: 21 Nm from MY2000, 18-24 Nm before that. Reconnect every hose, pipe, plug and fuel line, using your photos. Refit the air pipe.
steps.warn: The 4.2 manual table and EGR tube procedure say 20 Nm for that nut. Its intake manifold procedure alone says 60 Nm, which could strip a fine stud.

steps.title: Refit the supercharger
steps.text: Supercharged cars: refit the unit as in the supercharger coupler job.

steps.title: Refill and test
steps.text: Leave the battery off for at least 30 seconds in all, then reconnect the ground cable with one clean, firm contact and tighten to 4 Nm. Ignition on. Reset each window: hold the switch down for 5 seconds past the bottom stop, then up for 5 seconds past the top stop. Re-enter the radio code and set the clock. Prime the fuel system and check for leaks. Refill and bleed the coolant. Let the engine computer relearn: idle to full temperature, switch off, restart and idle for 2 minutes, hold 2 minutes in Drive on the brake, then drive about 5 miles of varied roads.

verify: No coolant loss on a pressure test
Idle stable with no vacuum leak
No knock sensor or throttle codes

diy.suits: A specialist, or a very experienced home mechanic. The intake manifold has to come off.
diy.stop: Stop if you lose track of a connection, or anything falls into an intake port.

items.title: Timing chain tensioners, AJ26 and AJ27
items.summary: The known 4.0 killer. The plastic secondary tensioners crack, and if a chain jumps two teeth the valves meet the pistons. The fix is metal-bodied tensioners, done with or without Jaguar's tools. Primary tensioners and guides mean the front cover comes off too.

parts.note: Metal body. LB and RB are mirror images, not interchangeable.
Reuse only if nearly new.
Only if the front cover comes off.
Only if the front cover comes off.

consumables: New coolant if the expansion tank is drained
New valve cover outer seals, bolt O-rings and plug well seals
Silicone gasket sealant to Jaguar specification
safety: Turn the crank clockwise only. Counter-clockwise can bind the chains.
Stuff a clean rag into the front of the cover opening. A dropped bolt in the sump is a disaster.
If a chain has jumped, stop. Do not crank the engine.
Never work under the car on a jack alone. Use stands on firm level ground, chock the wheels that stay down, and put the box in Park.
Do not jack on the aluminium front crossbeam, and do not lift the car by one front wheel. The crossbeam, steering rack and brake pipes can all be damaged.
Open a door so the glass drops before the battery goes off.

steps.title: Decide your method
steps.text: Method A follows JTIS: lock the cams, take the exhaust sprocket off, fit the tensioner. Method B leaves the sprocket on and lifts the exhaust cam: tie the chain to the sprocket, take off the exhaust cam caps, lift the cam, swap the tensioner. Method B needs no Jaguar tools. Jensen chose A because he wanted the cams firmly locked. Owners have done both.
steps.tip: Do one bank at a time.

steps.title: Doors open, battery off
steps.text: Open the driver's door, or both doors, so the frameless glass drops. Keep the doors open until the battery is disconnected. Then disconnect the battery ground cable in the boot.
steps.warn: With the glass still up and the battery off, shutting a door can foul the seal or the hood rail.

steps.title: Right bank access
steps.text: Remove the air intake. Take off the MAF plug, breather and two bolts over the throttle body, then remove the air box if needed. Rag over the throttle body. Remove the coil cover and coils.

steps.title: Left bank access
steps.text: Drain the coolant if the tank has to come off, or undo its top bolt and tie it aside. Remove the breather and dipstick tube nut. The tube can be stubborn on its stud. One owner cut the stud above the nut with a Dremel, and tie-wrapped the dipstick clear.
steps.tip: Check you can reach the lower rear cam cover bolt on the right bank before going further. It needs a short socket, universal joint and long extension.

steps.title: Cam covers off
steps.text: Remove the 14 cam cover bolts from the outside in, and lift the covers off. Cut the harness clips free if they will not release and refit with small ties. Stuff rag down into the front.

steps.title: Set the crank (method A)
steps.text: Remove the plugs so the engine turns freely. Raise the front safely on stands to reach the crank sensor on the flywheel housing, behind the sump. Remove its bolt and hang the sensor. Remove the torque converter access grommet. Turn the crank clockwise until the timing slot in the drive plate shows through the sensor hole and the cam timing flats are uppermost. Seat peg 303-531 fully in the slot and bolt it. Lower the car before fitting 303-530. Jensen took about 10 minutes to get it exact.
steps.warn: Clockwise only. Never rely on the jack alone while the sensor is off.
steps.tip: 303-531 is the 4.0 peg and 303-645 the 2003-on 4.2 tool. The Laser kit pin combines the two designs, so that kit does both.

steps.title: Lock the cams (method A)
steps.text: Check the flats on the right bank cams are facing up. If not, turn the crank 360 degrees. Fit locking bridge 303-530 across the cams. It stays on while you loosen or tighten sprocket bolts.

steps.title: Free the sprocket (method A)
steps.text: Tape a thin metal plate over the timing cover edge to protect the mating face. Fit a 10 mm ball-end hex in the sprocket bolt. Use 303-532 with a breaker bar to hold the sprocket against your wrench. Undo the bolt and slide the sprocket off the cam.
steps.warn: A flat hex will not reach, as the access is at an angle. Jensen countered the bolt with the Jaguar tool, and the 4.2 manual uses it the same way, but the Laser sheet says not to load its own version of that tool against sprocket bolts. Follow the note for the tool you own.

steps.title: Tie and unbolt (method B)
steps.text: Cable-tie the chain to the exhaust sprocket through the sprocket holes. Undo the five exhaust cam caps middle outward, one turn at a time, about 6 to 7 turns each. Keep them in order. Refit one cap bolt low at the rear to stop the cam rolling and twisting the chain.
steps.warn: Mark or keep the caps by their numbers and arrows. Do not forget to cut the tie at the end.

steps.title: Remove the tensioner
steps.text: Undo the two tensioner bolts and lift the old tensioner out. Tap gently if it sticks. Plastic ones have broken on removal, so check you have every fragment.
steps.check: Look for cracks above the notch at the base of the barrel, and inspect the slipper.

steps.title: Fit the new tensioner
steps.text: Clean the seat and keep the small oil hole between the bolt holes clear. Fit the new tensioner with the modified shorter bolts supplied for it, JFB 10607E in the bulletin, at 10-14 Nm. Do not reuse the old bolts. Right bank: the red pin comes out before fitting, so hold it together as you place it. Left bank: fit with the pin in, then pull it. Pour a little oil into the plastic runner hole.
steps.warn: Pull the red pin. Forgetting it leaves the chain slack. Check LB and RB markings.

steps.title: Reassemble (method A)
steps.text: Offer the sprocket up on the chain and set its position so tool 303-532 sits about vertical. From then on do not move the sprocket in the chain. Seat it and fit the bolt hand tight. Apply force on 303-532 anti-clockwise to tension the drive side of the chain, and hold that force while you tighten the bolt to 115-125 Nm.
steps.warn: The bolt has no key behind it, so this step sets the cam timing. The 4.2 figure of 20 Nm plus 90 degrees does not apply to a 4.0.

steps.title: Reassemble (method B)
steps.text: Oil the cam journals, keeping faces clean. Fit the five caps in order and bring them down evenly from the inside out to 10 Nm. Cut the tie. One write-up says 80 Nm for the caps: that is wrong, ignore it.
steps.warn: Cut the cable tie before closing up.

steps.title: Primary tensioners
steps.text: If you go further, the front cover has to come off, with the fan, belts, pulley, water pump pulley and power steering bracket. The damper bolt must be held with the pulley tool, never the crank peg. 4.0 figures: damper bolt 364-386 Nm with a split locking ring, or 80 Nm then a further 80 degrees without one. Primary tensioner bolts 10-14 Nm.
steps.warn: Tool and step detail here come from the 4.2 manual. The torques are 4.0 figures from JTIS.

steps.title: Check, then close up
steps.text: Remove the cam locks, rags and ties. Method A: raise the car on stands again and take the peg out. Turn the crank clockwise by hand through two full turns, then refit the peg and locks to prove the timing is unchanged, and take them off. Slack on the right bank with the bridge off can be normal, as Jensen found, and goes when the cams are set. Before fitting each cam cover, fit new seals, bolt O-rings and plug well seals, and apply a 3 mm by 12 mm bead of approved silicone at the two points where the head meets the front cover. Fit the cover straight down at once without smearing the bead. Tighten to 10 Nm, inside outward; MY2000 data says 11 Nm. Refit the crank sensor at the figure below for your car, then the grommet, plugs, coils and intake, and lower the car.

steps.title: Reconnect and relearn
steps.text: Leave the battery off for at least 30 seconds in all, then reconnect the ground cable with one clean, firm contact and tighten to 4 Nm. Ignition on. Reset each window: hold the switch down for 5 seconds past the bottom stop, then up for 5 seconds past the top stop. Re-enter the radio code and set the clock. Let the engine computer relearn: idle to full temperature, switch off, restart and idle for 2 minutes, hold 2 minutes in Drive on the brake, then drive about 5 miles of varied roads.

steps.title: First start
steps.text: Start and listen. Run to temperature and check for leaks around the cam covers. Metal tensioners can let you hear a faint chain sound that the plastic ones did not.

verify: Engine turns two full rotations by hand with no contact
No rattle on a cold start
No cam cover leak after a hot run

diy.suits: A specialist, or a very experienced home mechanic with the Jaguar setting tools. Get the timing wrong and the valves hit the pistons.
diy.stop: Stop if a chain has jumped. Do not crank the engine: have the car taken to a specialist.

items.title: Secondary chain tensioner, 4.2
items.summary: The factory job for the later engine, one bank at a time. Same cam lock and crank peg logic, but the sprocket bolt is a one-use torque-to-angle bolt with a Ribe head.

parts.note: Left and right are different.
One-use.

safety: Turn the crank clockwise only.
Fit a new sprocket bolt. Never reuse the old one.
Never work under the car on a jack alone. Use stands on firm level ground, chock the wheels that stay down, and put the box in Park.
Do not jack on the aluminium front crossbeam, and do not lift the car by one front wheel. The crossbeam, steering rack and brake pipes can all be damaged.
Open a door so the glass drops before the battery goes off.

steps.title: Doors open, battery off
steps.text: Open the driver's door, or both doors, so the frameless glass drops. Keep the doors open until the battery is disconnected. Then disconnect the battery ground cable in the boot.
steps.warn: With the glass still up and the battery off, shutting a door can foul the seal or the hood rail.

steps.title: Crank peg
steps.text: Raise the front safely on stands at the sill jacking points for access to the crank sensor. Remove the spark plugs so the engine turns freely. Unplug and remove the crank sensor.
