Turn the crank clockwise only, to 45 degrees after top dead centre on No. 1 cylinder, then fit peg 303-645. Lower the car.
steps.warn: Clockwise only. The timing chains can bind if the crank is turned backwards.

steps.title: Cam cover off
steps.text: Remove the valve cover on that bank, as in the coil and cover sections.

steps.title: Lock the cams
steps.text: Check the cam flats suit tool 303-530. If they do not, take the peg out, turn the crank a further 360 degrees clockwise and refit the peg. Fit 303-530 to the cylinder head.

steps.title: Remove the sprocket bolt
steps.text: Undo the exhaust sprocket bolt with Ribe socket 303-1077A. Discard it.

steps.title: Remove the tensioner
steps.text: Remove the two tensioner bolts. Move the sprocket and chain aside and lift the tensioner out.

steps.title: Fit the tensioner
steps.text: Fit the tensioner, then bring the sprocket and chain back. Tighten the bolts to 12 Nm and pull the retaining tool to release it.

steps.title: New sprocket bolt
steps.text: Fit a new bolt with the special tools, 20 Nm then a further 90 degrees.

steps.title: Close up
steps.text: Remove the locks and refit the valve cover at 10 Nm. Raise the car, take the peg out, refit the crank sensor and the spark plugs, and lower the car.

steps.title: Reconnect and relearn
steps.text: Leave the battery off for at least 30 seconds in all, then reconnect the ground cable with one clean, firm contact and tighten to 4 Nm. Ignition on. Reset each window: hold the switch down for 5 seconds past the bottom stop, then up for 5 seconds past the top stop. Re-enter the radio code and set the clock. Let the engine computer relearn: idle to full temperature, switch off, restart and idle for 2 minutes, hold 2 minutes in Drive on the brake, then drive about 5 miles of varied roads.

verify: No rattle on a cold start
No oil leak at the valve cover

diy.suits: A specialist, or a very experienced home mechanic with the Jaguar setting tools. Get the timing wrong and the valves hit the pistons.
diy.stop: Stop if the setting tools do not fit as the steps describe. Do not turn the engine until you know why.

items.title: Jacking points: lift the car and set it on stands
items.summary: Four sill plates are the only places to support the car: two just behind the front wheels, two just ahead of the rear wheels. The workshop jack goes under the front body crossmember, or under the rear subframe on a block of wood. Never on the aluminium suspension crossbeam, and never by one front wheel.
verify: The car sits square on all four stands before you go under it.
safety: Never rely on a jack alone. Use stands.
Stand the car on firm, level ground.
Do not rely on the parking brake alone: chock the wheels and put the box in Park.
Check the jack and stands are rated for the car.
Whenever possible use a ramp or pit instead of a jack.

steps.title: Know the four points
steps.text: The jacking points are reinforced plates on the sill flange, below the body side members. The front pair sit just behind the front wheels, the rear pair just ahead of the rear wheels. They also take the four pads of a wheel-free lift.

steps.title: Get ready
steps.text: Firm, level ground. Handbrake on, box in Park. Chock the wheels that stay down.

steps.title: Lift the front
steps.text: Put the workshop jack centrally under the front body crossmember, the steel crossmember at the very front that the towing eye screws into. Raise both front wheels together.
steps.warn: Never put the jack head on the aluminium suspension crossbeam, and never lift by one front wheel. The Vehicle Care book says not to use jacking equipment under the front cross member, without saying which one. Jaguar's workshop text puts the jack on the body crossmember and forbids the aluminium suspension crossbeam, so that is the one to keep off. No photo confirms this reading: if you cannot tell them apart, stop and read the Jacking page.

steps.title: Set the front stands
steps.text: Place stands at the two front jacking points and lower the car onto them.

steps.title: Lift the rear
steps.text: Put the jack centrally under the rear suspension subframe, with a block of wood between the jack head and the subframe. Raise the car.
steps.warn: Use the wood block.

steps.title: Set the rear stands
steps.text: Place stands at the two rear jacking points and lower the car onto them.

steps.title: With the car's own jack
steps.text: The jack in the boot is for changing a wheel and nothing else. Locate its groove fully on the sill plate at the nearest jacking point, and stop as soon as the tyre clears the ground.
steps.warn: With one rear wheel off the ground, Park does not hold the car. Chock the other wheels. Do not start the engine with the car on a jack, and never work under it.

diy.suits: Every owner who works on the car should learn this first.
diy.stop: Stop if the ground is soft or sloping, or the car moves on the stands. Lower it and start again.

items.title: Flat battery: open the boot, jump start or charge
items.summary: The battery is in the boot, and the boot latch release needs power. Open it with the black-headed key, then jump from the battery itself. No remote jump point is described in the handbooks. For a dead car that will not unlock, a boot that will not open and a car with nothing on the dash.
verify: The engine runs and the warning messages clear.
If it goes flat again, run the battery drain test.
safety: Never jump a battery that may be frozen.
The booster must be a 12 volt supply.
The two cars must not touch.
Hydrogen from a battery burns. No sparks or flames near it.
A car with this gearbox cannot be push or tow started.

steps.title: Open a door
steps.text: Use the key in the door lock. The fob and the buttons need battery power.

steps.title: Open the boot
steps.text: The keyhole is hidden in the badge on the back of the boot lid, on the right as you stand behind the car: between the X and the K of the name. Use the black-headed key: turn it 90 degrees clockwise, then back to vertical to take it out. The green-headed valet key will not open the boot.
steps.tip: The handbook says to disarm the alarm before using the key. Whether the alarm sounds with a flat battery is not stated.

steps.title: Reach the battery
steps.text: Lift out the boot floor panels, and on cars with one the right-hand side panel. Unclip the cover from the positive terminal.

steps.title: Prepare both cars
steps.text: Handbrake on and Park selected on both cars, all electrical items off. The cars must not touch. Do not run the donor car's engine: Jaguar warns that removing the leads with it running damages this car's electrics.
steps.warn: Follow the order exactly, and keep the booster to 12 volts.

steps.title: Connect the leads
steps.text: Red lead from booster positive to your battery positive. Black lead from booster negative to the spare wheel retaining bolt, which is the earth point and must be at least 305 mm (12 in) from the battery.
steps.warn: Do not connect the black lead to the negative terminal of the flat battery.

steps.title: Start and wait
steps.text: Start the car. Let it idle for five minutes before taking the leads off.

steps.title: Disconnect in reverse
steps.text: Black lead off the earth point, then off the booster. Red lead off both batteries. Clip the terminal cover back and refit the floor panels.

steps.title: Or charge it
steps.text: If you would rather charge it, connect a smart charger at the battery and follow the charger's instructions. Jaguar's books give no charging rate or time for this battery, so none is given here.
steps.warn: If you take the leads off the battery: ignition off first, negative lead off first, and partly open a window, because the door glass will not drop with the battery out.

steps.title: What resets afterwards
steps.text: If the battery was disconnected: the trip computer memories are wiped, the clock needs setting, the radio shows CODE and needs its security code, and the door windows must relearn their limits. Reset each window, ignition on: hold the switch down for 5 seconds past the bottom stop, then up for 5 seconds past the top stop. Wait at least 30 seconds between taking off the first lead and refitting the last. The message centre shows dashes until the bulb check ends. That is normal.

diy.suits: Any owner. The order of the leads is what matters.
diy.stop: Stop if the battery may be frozen, or it is swollen or leaking. Call roadside help.

needs: A second car or another 12 volt booster to start from

gaps: Main procedure source is Jaguar's 2003 to 2006 workshop manual, covering 4.2 cars from VIN A30645. JTIS v2.1 for MY1997-2004 is on disk and was read for the steps corrected in the audit: fuel filter, tensioners, gearbox level, dampers, belts, water pump, thermostat, radiator, alternator, starter and battery work. Other 4.0 steps still follow the 4.2 manual or owner write-ups. Jobs marked factory are factory for 4.2 cars unless a step says otherwise.
hoursBook is null on every job. Jaguar repair time schedules were not found. The manual gives operation numbers but no times.

hoursDiy is sourced for only a few jobs: tensioners about 7 h (Jensen), 4.0 thermostat housing 2 h (JagRepair), starter one day and intake manifold 8 h (owners). The rest are this project's estimates from step counts, not measured times.

Brake option: the pad jobs now follow the brake type you choose. The disc jobs are written for the standard sliding caliper. Brembo caliper removal for a disc change was not written up, so a Brembo car should follow its own manual there.

AJ26 versus AJ27 differences in tensioner work were not separated. JTIS has a 4.0 primary tensioner procedure that was not written up as steps here, so the primary tensioner step is a pointer with 4.0 torques only.

Conflicts in sources kept in step text: spark plug 27 vs 28 Nm, starter 45 vs 43 Nm, supercharger bolts 24, 20 and 21 Nm, intake manifold 22 vs 21 Nm, accessory idler bolt 45, 40 and 25 Nm, crank sensor 10 vs 7 Nm, diff fill 1.9 vs 1.8 L, 4.2 oil fill 7.0 L in the spec book vs 7.6 to 7.8 L from owners, and roof pump level marks (manual vs JagRepair).

Vee mounts: SNG Barratt's XK8 catalogue lists Vee mounting MJA2360AH, qty 2, and lists Subframe bush MJA2595A separately, so FCP's MJA2595AC looks like the rear subframe bush, as a Jaguar Forums reply also says. No factory procedure exists for the mount alone. The rear of the car has separate subframe mounts (A-frame bushes). The rear mount job was not written.

Gearbox: JTIS gives the W5A580 drain, refill and level steps and the 5HP24 level check, now in the job. JTIS does not give a 5HP24 filter change. 5HP24 pan and filter torques come from the ZF repair manual. W5A580 pan and filter service steps were not written up.

Propshaft: no factory coupling replacement exists, and the manual forbids disturbing it. No balancing procedure or 4.0 two-piece shaft notes were found. Model year of the change from one-piece to two-piece is from a single post. The myTo 1998 step limit is an inference from that post.
No torque found for: diff fill plug, crossover pipe bolts, supercharger nose bolts.

Supercharger coupler: Jaguar publishes no procedure. Nose bolt count and torque, sealant type and nose oil grade for the X100 M112 were not found. Later engine write-ups (5.0, 3.0) were used only for method, and are labelled as such. Whether the nose can be opened on the car is disputed. The factory route used here removes the unit.

Valley hose part numbers come from forum posts on a 1999 XK8 and vary by year. 4.0 intake manifold removal steps follow the 4.2 manual, so connector and hose details will differ. Supercharged valley access has no specific procedure.

Fuel filter: the fuse number for the owner method was reported by one owner (fuse 7, boot box, on a 2000 car). 4.0 filter fittings differ by year: JTIS shows threaded unions while owners report quick connectors on some early cars. Which VIN changes over was not found.
Starter: the rack-out route is JTIS MY2000. The rack-in shortcut is LHD owner reports only, and RHD access is unconfirmed. No 4.2 rack-out route was read.
Drain test: only the 30 mA and 60 minute figures are factory. The meter method is general electrical practice. The behaviour of the boot and door switches during sleep was not found for the X100.

Throttle body: no cleaning procedure in this manual. One owner quotes a 4.2 warning not to clean it, which this copy does not contain. Throttle body fixing torques: 10 Nm on 4.2 (manual), AJ26 18-24 Nm and AJ27 21 Nm (JagRepair).
Exhaust flange steps are 4.2 factory steps and were not cross-checked on a 4.0. JagRepair's alternator and throttle body cleaning pages are photos only and were not used.

Search budget ran out during this research. Later fetches used URLs already found. Jag-lovers XK library pages, JTIS and jagrepair HTTPS were refused or unreachable. Three Jaguar Owners Club threads returned 403 on direct fetch, so their claims rest on search result extracts.

Vee mounts: the method rests on one owner's 2006 Jag-lovers write-up, which worked on his car, with figures from the factory table. No second account of this route was found. The factory crossbeam lowering frees dampers, anti-roll links, engine mounts and front brackets instead. Whether the Torx sizes hold on later cars is not known: one poster says Torx up to at least 2000.

Jacking: JTIS 100-02, the same text from MY1997 to MY2004, puts the workshop jack under the front body crossmember and forbids the aluminium suspension crossbeam. The Vehicle Care book warns against jacking under 'the front cross member' without saying which. That warning is read here as the suspension crossbeam, but no photo confirms it. Handbooks describe the car's own jack for wheel changes only.
Valley hoses: MY2000-on NA and 4.2 evidence is absent. Bulletin 303-48a covers 1997-99 VIN 010343-042635 only.

Exhaust: JTIS prints "Information not available at this time" for the supercharged 4.0 converter and front silencer. The 4.0 steps come from the non-supercharged procedure. An owner video says all 4.0 cars have the slide fit, and the 4.0 supercharged clamp part number supports that, but no factory text confirms it for the XKR.

4.0 thermostat housing to block bolts: JTIS prints no figure in any year, only 8-10 Nm for the cover. Gearbox cooler pipes at the radiator: no figure for the non-supercharged 4.0, or for the XKR before MY2000.
